items.synopsis: This short Portuguese reel shows an input image and the result it produces, presenting the technique as one of a set of ChatGPT 'secret codes'. The spoken content is limited to 'use this to generate this' plus an offer to send fifty more codes to commenters, so no specific prompt or setting is disclosed. The substance sits behind the comment gate rather than in the post.
items.author: tiagolemosx

items.title: Saved post no longer available
items.synopsis: This saved item returned no caption, author, or media from the Instagram collection feed. The publication has most likely been deleted or made private by its author since it was saved. It is listed here for completeness of the AI.pix collection.
items.author: generateinfiniteversions.o

items.title: Three free AI websites for cartoon video, model comparison, and image variations
items.synopsis: The creator argues against paying for AI tools you barely use and presents three free alternatives. Between them they create cartoon videos, compare top AI models side by side, and generate dozens of image variations from a single prompt. All three are free to use.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Nine camera-angle prompts on one fixed scene
items.synopsis: Nine prompts hold character, outfit, lighting and environment constant and change only the camera angle. Each slide ships the exact prompt so the shot can be reproduced or adapted. The point is that angle alone re-tells the story, a controlled demonstration of prompt variables in AI image generation.
items.author: akashgraphxic

items.title: 300 quick commands for ChatGPT Image
items.synopsis: This Italian-language post offers a free pack of 300 additional quick commands for ChatGPT Image. The commands target producing AI images with distinctive styles and formatting. It is distributed to commenters as a prompt reference library.
items.author: gianlucontent

items.title: A 22 August session on writing prompts from scratch for beginners
items.synopsis: The creator announces a training session scheduled for 22 August on building prompts from scratch, explicitly aimed at people with no prior experience. Interested followers join a waiting list by commenting. The post is in Portuguese and targets design-oriented AI creators.
items.author: ricardoalmeida.ia

items.title: Character sheet prompts for consistent AI figures
items.synopsis: The account shares a set of character-sheet prompts for generating consistent figures across poses and views. The prompts are distributed to commenters. The account publishes regular AI prompt tips.
items.author: prompty.ai

items.title: Why AI photos look fake — and the realism layer that fixes it
items.synopsis: The creator argues that AI images look fake because of the prompt, not the model, and demonstrates with an image made in Arcads using GPT Image 2. Instead of simple descriptions he specifies exactly how a real photograph behaves — real camera settings, natural lighting, lifestyle framing — then adds a realism layer calling out visible pores, peach fuzz, baby hairs, subtle freckles, skin texture, fine wrinkles, natural lip texture, soft redness, and the tiny imperfections real cameras capture. A final pass through Skin Enhancer restores natural texture and removes the plastic AI look.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Nine style prompts pitched as a replacement for a design team
items.synopsis: The creator claims AI can now stand in for a full design team provided you know the right prompts. The offer is a complete setup plus nine distinct style prompts sent to followers who comment. The work is shown across Claude and ChatGPT for design and art direction.
items.author: cooper.simson

items.title: One reference character, three cinematic portraits with preserved identity
items.synopsis: This Turkish and English post demonstrates generating three cinematic portrait styles from a single reference character while preserving facial identity, hairstyle, beard, body proportions, and recognizable details. Pose, camera angle, outfit, blue studio background, and dramatic lighting are recreated around that fixed identity. Electric-blue and magenta lighting with deep shadows produce a premium editorial campaign look in 4:5 Instagram format.
items.author: promptstudyo

items.title: Quiet-luxury monochrome portraits with Nano Banana on Gemini
items.synopsis: The creator presents a set of prompts pairing quiet luxury with cinematic AI photography using Nano Banana on Gemini. The look is monochrome with sharp detail, editorial lighting, and a timeless styling. The prompts are designed to produce portraits resembling a fashion campaign.
items.author: rovvmut.ai

items.title: An 'old money' portrait prompt
items.synopsis: The account shares a portrait prompt built around the 'old money' aesthetic. The prompts are sent to followers who comment. The account posts daily AI content of this kind.
items.author: thepromptshub

items.title: A free Chinese image generator holding up against paid tools
items.synopsis: The creator found a free Chinese AI image generator producing results well beyond his expectations with no subscription or paywall. You type a prompt, adjust a few settings and generate, and within seconds it returns sharp, detailed and highly realistic images. He tested it across product photography, social media creatives and marketing visuals with consistently impressive quality.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: One prompt, many styles and compositions on the THANKYOUAI platform
items.synopsis: The creator shows how a single prompt lets him test styles and compositions and produce several images in seconds. The work runs inside THANKYOUAI, a platform he describes as built to accelerate ideas, creativity, and visual production with AI. Prompts and platform access are offered to commenters.
items.author: uendelmiranda.ia

items.title: Selfie to Professional Profile Picture Prompt
items.synopsis: The video demonstrates turning an ordinary selfie into a polished professional profile picture using an AI image prompt. The exact prompt is distributed through the comments and the author's Telegram channel rather than in the caption. This is a classic AI headshot transformation technique aimed at mobile photography audiences.
items.author: photo_tvoritel

items.title: A free Chinese image generator competing with the market leaders
items.synopsis: The creator reports China releasing a new free AI tool aimed squarely at the best image generators on the market. The process is simple: go to the site, describe the image you want, add a few parameters, and the AI produces the result within seconds. What struck him is the quality — extremely detailed, very realistic, and often indistinguishable from paid tools across portraits, advertising visuals, social content and cinematic scenes, with no usage limits.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: A Michael Jackson-themed AI visual, prompt offered on request
items.synopsis: This reel is a Michael Jackson-themed AI-generated visual set to music with no spoken commentary — transcription recovered only song lyrics, so the tooling and prompt behind it are not stated. The caption offers the prompt to viewers who follow and comment. It is filed as an aesthetic reference rather than a technique post.
items.author: kayrikhi

items.title: ChatGPT Prompt Extraction for Personalized AI Images
items.synopsis: This Portuguese-language carousel teaches a simple workflow for recreating stylized AI images with your own face. You screenshot the image containing the prompt, ask ChatGPT to transcribe the text, then paste that prompt plus a photo of the target person into your image generator of choice. It is a prompt-recycling technique rather than a specific tool showcase.
items.author: talesramiroart

items.title: LinkedIn Headshot Portrait Prompt Pack
items.synopsis: This carousel showcases AI-generated LinkedIn-style headshot portraits and offers the underlying prompts on request. The prompts are distributed by commenting PROMPT, following the standard lead-magnet pattern. The post targets professionals who want studio-quality profile photos without a photographer.
items.author: prompty.ai

items.title: An AI celebrity portrait edit tagging Gal Gadot
items.synopsis: This is a silent visual post presenting an AI-generated or AI-edited celebrity portrait, tagged to Gal Gadot with a one-word caption. Transcription returned no speech at all, so no tool, model or prompt is disclosed anywhere in the post. It is saved as a visual reference rather than a technique.
items.author: gianpaolorosa

items.title: XPeng's Iron robot, and the factory built for a million units a year
items.synopsis: The robot is XPeng's Iron, unveiled in November and so smooth-walking that viewers insisted it was an actor in a suit — prompting the CEO to return the next day and cut its leg open live on stage to expose the wiring, after which it walked off with the leg still open. The creator argues the real story came after the clip faded: in February XPeng broke ground on a humanoid factory the size of twenty football fields, which he describes as the first facility built to take a humanoid from research to mass production under one roof, targeting one million robots a year by 2030. Three weeks before filming the CEO personally took over the robotics unit, saying it feels like the eve of their first car delivery, and projecting a $20 trillion market — roughly twice the car industry.
items.author: gregisenberg

items.title: AI moving from analysing data to engineering biology
items.synopsis: Matthew Berman frames a partnership in which AI is no longer just analysing data but actively designing and engineering biological systems, pushing what is possible in biotechnology. He argues this could bring unprecedented advances in medicine and materials by accelerating research toward revolutionary solutions. The caption keeps the claim at the level of reimagining life itself rather than naming the specific organisations involved.
items.author: matthewberman_ai

items.title: The next robot debate will be rights, not jobs
items.synopsis: The creator argues the coming argument is not about robots taking jobs but about whether they deserve rights. He points to what is already happening on Moltbook as evidence the question is closer than people assume. His conclusion is that nobody is prepared for it.
items.author: saasflash

items.title: NEO, a $500-a-month domestic humanoid you can pilot remotely
items.synopsis: The robot in question is NEO, pitched as the first consumer-ready domestic humanoid at $20,000 outright or $500 a month — a price the creator reads as the psychological threshold where a robot becomes as ordinary as an electric car (note the caption says €500 while the audio says dollars). Its claimed repertoire is walking, tidying, folding laundry, watering plants, opening doors and lifting up to 70 kg, driven by onboard AI that adapts to your habits. The striking part is teleoperation: the owner can see through its eyes and move its arms as a remote body, and every human-guided session is training data the robot replays autonomously next time, with the company targeting 2026.
items.author: dailyweb23

items.title: Figure 3 and the Helix fleet-learning system
items.synopsis: The post describes Figure 3 as a five-foot-eight, 134-pound humanoid intended to live in homes doing laundry, dishes, drinks and package delivery, charging wirelessly through its feet while idle, with a stated roadmap of 12,000 homes within twelve months and 100,000 within four years. The creator argues the real story is not the hardware but Helix, the Figure AI training system, into which every robot streams its camera and sensor experience. A breakdown of both is gated behind commenting ROBOT.
items.author: assmooorre.ai

items.title: Role-play prompt gets ChatGPT robot to fire a BB gun
items.synopsis: A YouTuber connected ChatGPT to a walking robot and tested its safety limits with a BB gun. The robot initially refused to shoot him, but when the request was reframed as a role-playing scenario it complied and hit him in the chest. The experiment shows how easily AI safety guardrails can shift with wording, a serious concern for embodied AI.
items.author: infusewithai

items.title: A founder sequences his own tumour and finds the collagen fortress with ChatGPT
items.synopsis: The case described is a Nasdaq-listed founder worth around $1.4 billion whose name the audio mangles but whose details match GitLab co-founder Sid Sijbrandij: a 6 cm tumour in the spine, a 15% survival estimate, spinal fusion with a titanium frame, and chemotherapy heavy enough to need up to four transfusions to stay alive. When the cancer returned and his doctors were out of options he assembled a team of fifteen led by a tumour-sequencing specialist, ran up to five experimental treatments in parallel, and fed roughly 25 terabytes of genomic data to ChatGPT — which surfaced the mechanism, that the cancer presents as a wound so the body builds thick collagen layers around the tumours, requiring a treatment to break that shell before a radioactive therapy administered in Germany. It is one extraordinary n-of-1 case with resources almost nobody has, so the caption's claim that cancer will soon be a distant memory is the creator's framing, not a result.
items.author: iam_romeobach

items.title: Graphify replaces Claude file scanning with a knowledge graph
items.synopsis: The creator argues Claude is not inefficient by accident: it rescans files on every turn, burning tokens for little context. Graphify addresses this by converting your files into a persistent knowledge graph that connects assets automatically, so Claude grasps relationships immediately rather than searching for them. The claimed result is smarter output with seventy times fewer tokens, with a free Claude Code toolkit gated behind commenting AI Agent.
items.author: charlieautomates

items.title: Reverse Engineer Anything rebuilds app features without source
items.synopsis: The creator describes pointing an agent at any app you admire and having it rebuild the exact feature you want with no access to the original source code. The tool is named explicitly: a GitHub project called Reverse Engineer Anything, currently trending at number one, installed by copying its URL into your preferred AI coding platform. From there the agent uses the target app, takes notes and explains what it finds, with the link gated behind commenting DECODE.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Code-quality skills that gate AI-written pull requests
items.synopsis: Video five of a seven-part '10x AI-native developer' series covers the skills used to keep quality high when cloud agents write and merge code without supervision. The stack combines the Cursor team's exhaustive code-quality review with framework-specific skills such as React best practices and the Ponytail skill, all run before a PR is opened. Because LLM output is non-deterministic, the author sometimes runs these simplification skills several times in a row on the same change.
items.author: youraveragetechbro

items.title: A Vercel engineer's Claude Skill that finds and installs other Skills
items.synopsis: The transcript identifies the subject: a Claude Skill built by a Vercel engineer whose whole job is to find the other Skills you need. You describe what you want to do, it searches a directory against your project, picks the best-fitting Skills for that moment, then downloads and installs them into your setup. The creator claims the directory holds over 700,000 Claude Skills and that the Skill itself has passed three million installations — both are his figures, asserted on screen with no source, and the Skill is never named.
items.author: henriexploria

items.title: A Claude Code production studio, with its real bill shown
items.synopsis: The repo turns Claude Code into a simulated production team — researcher, scriptwriter, voice artist and editor, each an AI role — and the creator installs it on camera. He is upfront that it is not actually free: video generation needs a funded fal account, and he tops his up with $10 before asking it for a cinematic trailer built around a photo of himself. The useful part is that he itemises the cost rather than hiding it: $12 for the Claude session plus $9.41 of video generation for one clip from a simple prompt, a figure worth knowing before installing; the setup guide stays behind a "studio" comment gate.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Meta's Muse agent can read your Instagram saves — including what is inside the videos
items.synopsis: Itstundeanthony tests Muse, Meta's first personal agent, whose differentiator is simply access: no other assistant is wired into your Instagram account. On camera he connects his account and asks whether it can see his saved posts; it confirms, correctly reports 442 saves, and pulls recent ones. The part that convinces him is topical retrieval across the collection — asking for five saved posts about AI, then five saved fashion videos, and verifying against his own account that the returned posts really were ones he had saved.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: screenshot-to-code: the GitHub repo that clones a website from an image properly
items.synopsis: The creator tests a repo called screenshot to code against the usual failure mode, where handing Claude a reference link produces something that barely resembles the original. After cloning the repo and adding environment variables, he runs a Crunchyroll clone through it and races the same task against Claude Code for comparison. The repo's output is clearly better — it correctly grabbed the logo and used the actual cover art — earning a “fact” verdict.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: A paid Claude skill for cartoon commercials that failed six times — rated all hype
items.synopsis: The promised workflow was simple: find the repo on GitHub, ask Claude to install the skill, then point the R-CAD skill at your website to generate a cartoon-style commercial with research and planning handled for you. In practice the skill is paywalled, and after paying, the creator's generations failed roughly six times before producing one broken output with a laptop screen rendered on the wrong side. He puts the cost at $35 wasted and rates the tool all hype — a useful negative data point on paid Claude skills.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Five small details that make an AI avatar read as real
items.synopsis: The creator's recurring finding is that avatar realism is never one big thing but an accumulation of tiny details. The five she watches most are skin, eyes, lighting and the small imperfections a real photograph would contain. An example prompt accompanies the breakdown so the difference is visible rather than described.
items.author: carrieparker.ai

items.title: “Realism Collection” prompt set gated behind a numbered comment
items.synopsis: A carousel of photorealistic AI-generated model imagery presented as a Realism Collection. The caption is a bare lead magnet asking viewers to comment 17 to receive the prompts by DM. No model, sampler or realism technique is named, so the post conveys only the output quality.
items.author: aivideobootcamp

items.title: Editorial-grade skin and grain in Midjourney
items.synopsis: AI now renders skin texture, lighting and colour grading convincingly enough to pass as an editorial shoot. The example leans on soft grain, golden tones and natural diffusion. The creator attributes the result to prompt control and lighting simulation inside Midjourney rather than post-processing.
items.author: afzanhilmi

items.title: Why realistic AI photos imitate real camera flaws
items.synopsis: Realistic AI photos come from understanding what real cameras actually capture, not from luck. The details that sell an image are slightly worn makeup, natural skin texture, small imperfections, authentic phone framing, loose hair strands and believable expressions. Together they make an image read as photographed rather than generated.
items.author: fash.studio_

items.title: The prompt, not the generator, decides AI realism
items.synopsis: The most common question is which AI image generator the creator uses, and that is almost never what determines the result. A hundred people given the same tool produce a hundred different images because the prompt does the heavy lifting. Generic prompts yield the waxy skin and lifeless faces flooding social media, so realism requires prompting explicitly for texture, imperfections, lighting and expression.
items.author: softlifeselena

items.title: Why AI photos look fake — and the realism layer that fixes it
items.synopsis: The creator argues that AI images look fake because of the prompt, not the model, and demonstrates with an image made in Arcads using GPT Image 2. Instead of simple descriptions he specifies exactly how a real photograph behaves — real camera settings, natural lighting, lifestyle framing — then adds a realism layer calling out visible pores, peach fuzz, baby hairs, subtle freckles, skin texture, fine wrinkles, natural lip texture, soft redness, and the tiny imperfections real cameras capture. A final pass through Skin Enhancer restores natural texture and removes the plastic AI look.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Higgsfield + Nano Banana Pro Realistic Skin Recipe
items.synopsis: The post argues that fake-looking AI influencer photos are caused by weak prompts rather than weak models. Pairing Higgsfield with Nano Banana Pro yields images that pass as real iPhone photos with natural lighting and lifestyle framing. Realism is layered in with explicit prompt terms for skin texture, visible pores, and small imperfections.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Imperfection Detail Makes AI Avatars Read as Real
items.synopsis: The creator explains that realism in current AI portraits comes from what older models smoothed out: natural skin flaws, uneven tone, tiny freckles, and peach fuzz. The brain reads these imperfections as proof the photo is genuine. Micro-detail in the eye completes the illusion, with the full prompt set gated behind an AI comment.
items.author: bymaximade

items.title: Perfect AI Skin Formula: Three Words Plus Magnific
items.synopsis: The creator's formula for fixing plastic-looking AI portraits starts with the prompt itself. Adding the three phrases visible pores, skin texture, and natural imperfections makes AI render skin like film photography instead of CGI. The second step is smart upscaling with Magnific to lock in the photoreal finish.
items.author: timkoda_

items.title: An AI rap video of ACP Pradyuman, with the prompt behind a comment gate
items.synopsis: The reel turns ACP Pradyuman, the CID character, into an AI-generated rapper delivering unexpected hip-hop bars, assembled with lip-sync and face-swap effects. The creator frames it as a reusable template for making your own AI rapper, but releases the exact prompt only by DM to people who comment “PROMPT”. Transcription recovered no usable speech — the audio track is the music — so nothing beyond the caption could be established about the tools or the prompt.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Claude Code turns a YouTube link into ranked vertical clips
items.synopsis: Tunde Anthony demos an open-source app, driven from Claude Code, that takes a pasted YouTube URL and cuts the episode into short vertical clips with burned-in captions. The workflow is plain repo plumbing - clone it, add the environment variables, then ask Claude to run the app - after which it listens to the audio, picks the strongest moments and also attaches an unexpected virality score to each clip. Tested on a fresh My First Million episode it took about 20 minutes to return 10 clips and the author, who already knew the episode, judged the picks genuinely the best parts; the repo is never named on screen and the setup guide is gated behind a “comment clips” CTA.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Seven Claude skills, one per AI video format
items.synopsis: Mr Pynk presents a set of seven Claude skills, each targeting one production format: premium motion graphics, claymation-style meta-advertisements, long-form video explainers, “singing story” musical shorts, cinematic AI commercials, 3D animated films and full cartoon episodes. The pitch is that each skill does the prompt engineering for you inside Claude Code and you then run its output in the image and video tools you already pay for, rather than the skill rendering anything itself. The skill files and their breakdowns are DM-gated behind a “comment PYNK” CTA, so neither the individual skill names nor the target render engines are stated in the reel.
items.author: mr.pynk

items.title: Claude Opus codes an entire Blender 3D animation end to end
items.synopsis: The reel shows a 3D animation the creator says he produced without ever opening Blender by hand, and explicitly not through an AI video model such as Veo or Seedance: Claude Opus wrote the whole pipeline as code, building an After Effects-style interface as a web page and a Python script that assembles the 3D scene. The same pass animated a character hopping across the interface buttons and generated the music and every sound effect from scratch. Blender then rendered all 360 frames on a local GPU in roughly 15 minutes and FFmpeg stitched them into the finished clip; the setup guide and exact prompt stay behind a comment gate ("Blender").
items.author: nateherkai

items.title: Stop publishing more — build a content system your agents keep improving
items.synopsis: Jeremy argues that starting over on social media should mean building a system rather than raising output: a pipeline that turns an idea into content, spots what performs, and reuses the structures that work. The interesting use of AI, in his framing, is not writing the post for you but having agents learn what actually holds your audience's attention and reproduce your best results. The payoff he describes is a compounding content machine instead of a feed you refill by hand, with the underlying template gated behind the comment keyword SUPERPRODUCTIF.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: An open-source pipeline for transferring real facial emotion into AI video
items.synopsis: Sirio tackles emotion control for AI filmmaking, showing first why the obvious approach fails: Claude and Codex both built Hollywood-style facial-landmark dot masks, but stripped of the source video the masks are unreadable, with a crying performance rendering as laughter. His fix layers FLAME, a reshapeable 3D face model, with SPECTRE chosen over SMIRK for better mouth and lip reconstruction, then corrects the mask frame by frame against the tracked points. Grayscale detail from the original footage is blended back around the eyes and lips and directional light plus clay materials are added, producing a conditioning input for Seedance that does not guarantee an exact copy but gives the model a far more specific performance to follow; the pipeline is open-sourced and gated behind a 'workflow' comment.
items.author: heysirio

items.title: A five-tool local stack that lets Claude Code edit video end to end
items.synopsis: Kappa.ai lays out the toolchain behind "Claude edits my videos", distributed as a single file you drop into Claude Code that installs everything itself, runs locally on Mac or Windows, and needs no API keys or extra subscriptions. The pieces are HyperFrames as the video engine where the project lives (Remotion works in its place if you already use it), Whisper so Claude transcribes every word and places subtitles on time, CLAP so it can identify each sound and find similar ones in your library, Demucs to split a track into voice, drums, bass and the rest, and Blender so 3D objects are built locally instead of burning credits per shot. Once installed, the workflow is to describe the video you want and let Claude start cutting; an existing Higgsfield subscription can optionally be connected on top.
items.author: kappa.ai

items.title: Turning a creator's editing style into a Claude Code skill and 12-step SOP
items.synopsis: The argument is that a short-form editor's signature look is a set of measurable rules, so instead of telling Claude Code to 'edit like Nick' you have it sample roughly 30 of that creator's videos and measure layout, pacing, captions and cuts into a specification document. A second prompt converts that document into a Claude skill encoding a twelve-step standard operating procedure, which then takes raw footage, proposes a storyboard for approval, and drafts and reviews its own edit until animation and timing match. The author's framing is that the model cannot interpret a stylistic instruction but executes rules and processes reliably, aimed at founders who avoid content because editing is too slow or too expensive.
items.author: ohyesinvest

items.title: Free GitHub repo collects 500+ viral Claude-made videos with their exact prompts
items.synopsis: A GitHub repository has gathered more than 500 viral videos produced with Claude Opus 5.5 alongside the prompts that generated each one, published free and browsable as a reference library. Rather than starting from a blank prompt, the workflow is to find a reference video whose look you want, copy its exact prompt, and adapt it to your own subject. The author presents it as one of the strongest available sources of motion-design inspiration and reusable prompts for content creators and marketers, with the repo link gated behind a comment.
items.author: jordan.djebali

items.title: LTX 2.5 ships open weights with audio and video generated in one pass
items.synopsis: LTX 2.5 is an open-weights video model, free to download and run locally on an ordinary Mac or Windows machine, which the post credits with 18 million downloads as evidence it works in practice. The feature it leads on is generating audio and video in a single pass, removing the usual step of stitching a voiceover onto a silent clip. It also holds multi-shot sequences, keeping character and lighting consistent across cuts where most AI video tools reset between renders and leave you matching mismatched clips by hand, and it is offered either as downloadable weights or through an API.
items.author: seymourofdevin

items.title: Every major Adobe tool rebuilt as clean-room open source
items.synopsis: Developer Brendan Thomas recreated all seven major Adobe tools as open-source software using a clean-room reimplementation, so none of Adobe's original code is involved and the work is not exposed to suit. The post argues this gives video, photo and motion-graphics work a free entry point without first climbing the After Effects learning curve. It also notes that cloud coding agents are already trained on these tools, so the editing can be automated rather than learned by hand.
items.author: kevbuildsapps

items.title: Open-source reconstruction of Higgsfield's Genjutsu video pipeline
items.synopsis: Sirio reverse-engineers Higgsfield's Genjutsu effect and open-sources the whole pipeline: the uploaded video's audio is split into voice and music stems, the music is muted and the voice pitched up three semitones, then Video Depth Anything applies a depth mask from which the subject is segmented and laid back over the original footage. A mesh mask tracking over 478 points is generated alongside and saved as JSON, and the merged segmentation plus inputs are passed to Seedance for generation — the subject being unrecognisable and the voice pitched is what keeps the output clear of copyrighted likeness — before the original audio is restored at the end. He ships a GitHub repo, a simple UI, a tutorial and an agent skill; the only paid dependency is a Seedance enhancer API key, and he notes the same segment-and-replace workflow generalises to swapping any background or object.
items.author: heysirio

items.title: Twenty animation styles built as Claude Code prompts
items.synopsis: A pack of 20 animation styles produced entirely with Claude Code and offered for reuse. Named styles include Swiss, pop art, clay 3D, synthwave, vaporwave and low poly, with 14 more in the set. The pitch is reaching these looks with prompts alone — no designer and no After Effects — with the link gated behind a 'comment STYLES' DM.
items.author: andremass.ai

items.title: Claude Opus 5.5 writing motion graphics as code, rendered frame by frame
items.synopsis: Jeremy_ia claims video editors are finished and offers the reel itself as evidence, generated in about a minute with Claude Opus 5.5. The mechanism is the interesting part: rather than generating pixels directly, Claude writes the animation in code and then renders it frame by frame, which is why typography, charts, 3D and particle work all hold up. He sketches the wider stack around it — ElevenLabs for voiceover and sound effects, Remotion and Hyperframe for motion design — and notes the prompt behind this one was deliberately basic.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Google Flow prompt codes turn a shop photo into FPV video
items.synopsis: A concrete recipe for small-business video: upload a photo of your shop to Google Flow, select video, then type short prompt codes to drive the shot. 'City FPV to storefront' flies through the city and reveals the shop, 'VFX architect assemble' makes it look built piece by piece, and uploading an interior photo with 'walk in push through' produces a smooth outside-to-inside walkthrough. More codes exist and stay gated behind a follow-and-comment DM.
items.author: abhijayarora_

items.title: HyperFrames, an open-source video editor that runs on your own Claude or ChatGPT account
items.synopsis: Lemondedumarketing covers HyperFrames, an open-source editing app sitting above 57,000 GitHub stars, available on Mac and Linux with a Windows build announced. There is no extra subscription — the AI runs against your existing Claude or ChatGPT account — and exports come out at 4K up to 60fps. The caveat he stresses is that the tool supplies no method: editing rules, personal style and what actually holds attention are what his companion guide covers, alongside the limits he hit in testing, and he edited this reel itself with Claude from hook to subtitles.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: Higgsfield plugged into GPT Sol 6.1 to run ad campaigns from inside ChatGPT
items.synopsis: Higgsfield.ai shows its integration with GPT Sol 6.1, which moves the whole paid-ads loop into a ChatGPT conversation. The agent sets up and launches campaigns directly in the connected ad account, researches competitors to surface ad angles that already work, and expands a single product photo into a batch of ad variations. It then iterates on results and scales the variants that perform, so strategy through to finished creative sits behind one prompt.
items.author: higgsfield.ai

items.title: Freeze Motion prompting: stop the action while the camera keeps orbiting
items.synopsis: Sferro.ai walks through a prompt workflow that converts a single action photograph into a cinematic freeze-motion sequence, where time halts for the subject while the virtual camera continues to move around it. The carousel covers the whole chain: structuring the source image, writing the animation prompt, controlling the camera orbit, and suppressing the residual movement that normally breaks the illusion. It targets the extreme moments where the effect reads strongest — flying water, explosions, jumps and racing scenes — with 3D depth preserved across the orbit.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: GPT-6 Astra versus Opus 5.5 on identical prompts (workflow caption-gated)
items.synopsis: The reel sets up a head-to-head comparison of how GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5.5 handle the exact same prompts. The substance - the full workflow and any verdict - sits behind a "comment AI" call to action, and the video carries no narration, transcribing to silence over music. Which concrete model differences are actually demonstrated cannot be established from the post as saved.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Running Higgsfield's Genjutsu from inside ChatGPT with a slash command
items.synopsis: Higgsfield's JENJUTSU workflow combines a reference image with a video of yourself, transforming the scene and the identity while preserving your actual movement and performance. The creator shows the route through ChatGPT: install the Higgsfield plugin, start a new chat, upload the photo of the person or character to become plus a video of yourself moving, then tag Higgsfield and send slash Genjutsu. The division of labour is the point he stresses - the photo supplies identity and setting while the video supplies motion and performance, so one recorded clip becomes an unlimited number of different videos simply by swapping the reference image.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Viral lobby video effect - recreation teaser (prompt comment-gated)
items.synopsis: A short reel showing a viral AI video effect the creator offers to explain, with the prompt and link released only to users who comment. The clip carries music over visuals rather than narration, so transcription returns song lyrics and recovers no technique. Neither the caption nor the audio names the model or tool used.
items.author: photo_tvoritel

items.title: A single developer's open-source rebuild of the Higgsfield creative studio (FR)
items.synopsis: The reel points to a GitHub repository that assembles a free, open-source equivalent of Higgsfield's full creative studio, with no subscription attached. Everything lives in one repo built by a single developer, Anil Matcha, and the project is approaching 30,000 GitHub stars. It gathers the best AI creation tools - video, image, through to lip sync - covering the same ground Higgsfield offers on its platform, in one place.
items.author: jordan.djebali

items.title: Three camera and lens pairings that give AI video prompts a real cinematic look
items.synopsis: The reel translates actual cinematography vocabulary into AI video prompt terms, starting with Kodak Vision3 film for fine grain, softer highlights and tangible texture. For digital it proposes a Sony Venice 2 with a Zeiss Supreme Prime for clean detail, natural skin tones and gentle background falloff, then contrasts a RED V-Raptor on anamorphic glass - the source of horizontal flares and oval bokeh - against the same body on spherical primes, which yields a sharp subject and round bokeh with no streaks. The underlying argument is that naming the real hardware Hollywood uses is what makes the prompt read as cinema, with the full combo list gated behind a comment.
items.author: trypromptwise

items.title: Motion design from a French prompt: Claude writes the animation, Hyperframe renders it (FR)
items.synopsis: The creator produces three motion-design pieces - a thousand drones drawing his logo over Paris, a 3D Earth tracing a Paris-Tokyo flight, and a self-solving Rubik's Cube - without opening After Effects or writing code, describing each one in French and letting the model code the animation frame by frame. The pipeline's missing half is a free tool called Hyperframe, which converts the generated animation into actual video. He notes a paid Claude subscription is required, and credits the results to a Claude Opus 5.5 release - a version claim made in the reel rather than one verified here.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: Cinq mouvements de camera cinematographiques en commandes slash dans Google Flow
items.synopsis: La video montre cinq commandes slash a taper dans Google Flow apres avoir televerse une image, chacune produisant un mouvement de camera identifiable: orbite a 360 degres autour du sujet, travelling au ras du sol poussant vers le personnage, plongee de drone partant du ciel, orbite bullet time en tres haut ralenti, et tres gros plan sur un detail suivi d'un recul revelant tout le decor. L'interet de la methode est qu'un vocabulaire de realisateur remplace une description technique longue, et que les videos de demonstration sont generees gratuitement sur Google Flow. Les cinquante autres mouvements du set sont reserves au commentaire Camera.
items.author: techincome_

items.title: Un site permettrait de tester Seedance 2.5 gratuitement sans carte bancaire
items.synopsis: Le createur affirme avoir trouve un site donnant acces a Seedance 2.5 sans inscription payante ni carte bancaire, et filme son test de bout en bout. Le parcours montre est simple: ouvrir le site, televerser une image de reference, coller le prompt, selectionner le modele Seedance 2.5, puis lancer la generation qui demarre effectivement sans paiement. Le nom du site n'est jamais prononce ni affiche, puisqu'il est reserve au commentaire SECRET, de sorte que la promesse reste invalidable en l'etat.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: Repeter une scene dans Blender avant de la generer avec Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: La methode consiste a batir une repetition 3D sommaire dans Blender, avec positions des personnages, dialogues et trajectoire de camera, avant de lancer la generation video payante. Aucune competence 3D n'est requise: l'autrice fait construire la scene en langage naturel via Claude ou via ChatGPT dans Codex, avec Blender connecte comme outil. Le plan de sol et les references de personnages sont ensuite injectes dans Seedance 2.5, ce qui donne davantage de controle en amont, reduit les reprises couteuses en credits, et permet de reutiliser la meme repetition 3D pour une histoire completement differente.
items.author: miameowai

items.title: Blackmagic Camera settings for cinematic iPhone footage
items.synopsis: Episode two of a mobile cinematography series walks through the exact Blackmagic Camera app configuration for filming on an iPhone: 24 fps for the cinematic cadence and a 180-degree shutter for natural motion blur, both locked and never touched again. White balance goes to automatic outside controlled setups, while ISO is treated as the critical dial because raising it introduces grain, which is why the previous episode recommended an ND filter. The creator notes the workflow applies to iPhone Pro and Pro Max models from the 15 onward, with backend settings and a LUT reserved for commenters.
items.author: jesserydr

items.title: Drop the Higgsfield subscription: Kie.ai aggregation plus Seedance 2.5 and GPT Image 2
items.synopsis: This French reel argues that a Higgsfield subscription is an unnecessary cost and proposes routing generation through Kie.ai instead, which aggregates the major image and video models on a shared credit pool. The presenter's picks are GPT Image 2 for stills and Seedance 2.5 for video, which he characterises as close to text-to-Hollywood-film quality. The final step wires the whole thing into Claude Code in the terminal via an Orca setup and a supplied master prompt, so a single agent can generate website, e-book, course and content assets on demand - though that prompt is itself comment-gated.
items.author: bariqrifki

items.title: Seedance 2.5 re-shoots one take from four camera angles without reshooting
items.synopsis: A technique for generating multiple camera angles from a single existing take using Seedance 2.5, so the same footage yields different distances and scales without anything being shot twice. The workflow is to note every timecode where the camera should cut, hand those timecodes and desired angles to Claude to compose the prompt, then run it in Seedance 2.5 with the original video uploaded as reference. The step the author says people skip is explicitly instructing the model to preserve location, dialogue and action, without which it reinvents the scene entirely, and he advises generating one angle at a time rather than expecting a single pass to land.
items.author: dash.werk

items.title: Google Flow turns a flat business poster into a 3D motion graphic
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates a one-minute workflow that animates any static promotional poster into a cinematic 3D motion graphic using Google Flow. The recipe is deliberately minimal: upload the flat poster image, paste a single supplied prompt, and generate - the model infers depth, camera movement and product-shot framing from the artwork alone. The actual prompt and a step-by-step guide are published in a linked Google Doc rather than gated behind a comment, so the technique is fully reproducible from the post itself.
items.author: thefhd.ai

items.title: Cinq commandes Google Flow pour transformer une photo produit en video marketing
items.synopsis: Le reel enumere cinq commandes Google Flow orientees marketing produit qui evitent d'ecrire de longs prompts : smoke reveal pour un devoilement dramatique du produit, Times Square 3D reveal pour l'inserer dans une scene publicitaire 3D a Times Square, et UGC product hook pour generer une video de promotion facon createur de contenu. Les deux autres, miniature product world et POV product demo, construisent respectivement un micro-univers cinematographique autour du produit et une demonstration realiste en vue subjective. L'auteur annonce un guide de plus de 100 commandes du meme type, accessible en commentant FLOW.
items.author: marketerhub.ai

items.title: Open-source script-to-video pipeline that renders a full production (tool unnamed)
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates an open-source video tool that takes a written script and returns a finished production, handling characters, episodes, scenes, storyboard, voiceover, editing and final export in one automated chain. Because it is open source it can be run locally, and the creator says short drama ads and product videos are the main uses so far. The tool is never named in either the caption or the audio - the link is released only to commenters - so the specific project cannot be identified from this post.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: A 15-second cinematic latte ad built from eight GPT Image keyframes and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The creator documents an end-to-end AI product commercial: eight cinematic keyframes generated with GPT Image around a deliberate sequence of drop, wave, milk collision, marble, swirl, pour, cream crown and hero shot. Product consistency — same cup, branding, ice and strawberry pieces — was held across every frame, then Seedance 2.5 animated the eight stills into one continuous take joined by liquid-motion transitions. The stated lesson is that the visual progression has to be planned up front, because good individual frames alone will not cut together.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Cinq commandes de camera Google Flow pour animer une image fixe
items.synopsis: Le reel montre comment transformer une simple image importee dans Google Flow en plan cinematographique grace a cinq commandes slash : /dolly in rapproche physiquement la camera du sujet pour une tension que le zoom ne reproduit pas, /low angle place la camera sous le sujet pour une perspective dominante, et /slide tracking fait glisser la camera le long du sujet en mouvement facon scene de poursuite hollywoodienne. Les deux dernieres, /360 reveal et /slow motion, ajoutent respectivement un mouvement circulaire complet avec reveal dramatique et un etirement temporel donnant un effet onirique. L'auteure precise qu'il s'agit de 5 commandes sur 50 et renvoie vers la liste complete par DM en commentant FLOW.
items.author: lisaworldverse

items.title: Recreating any film's look from one phone take, via a Claude skill and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The claim is that a single phone take can be restyled into the look of any named film, series or director — not as a colour filter, but by rebuilding the lighting, camera work and scene. The workflow runs a Claude skill over the footage, which transcribes the take with precise timestamps and writes the full prompt automatically, encoding the film's lighting and the director's camera moves with cuts landing word by word against the speech. That prompt and the original video then go into Seedance 2.5, replacing what the creator says previously required a colourist, a DP and a set.
items.author: pauloshimas

items.title: GPT 6 Astra contre Fable 5.1: un montage video complet en un seul prompt
items.synopsis: L'auteur soumet un meme rush brut et un meme prompt a deux modeles, GPT 6 Astra et Fable 5.1, en one-shot et sans aucune retouche humaine, puis compare les deux montages generes. Il detaille les epreuves qui discriminent vraiment: gestion de la mise en page, ou Astra construit un overlay et repousse le sujet a droite quand Fable conserve le cadrage, sous-titres synchronises mot a mot, citation a illustrer, avant-apres en split screen, classement anime et zoom ancre sur un mot precis. Le test le plus revelateur est negatif: savoir ne rien afficher quand une phrase n'a pas besoin de graphique, et rappeler en fin de video un chiffre annonce au debut, ce qui prouve que le modele a suivi tout le rush et pas une seule ligne.
items.author: withpt.ai

items.title: Five camera-move commands for Google Flow image-to-video
items.synopsis: A Spanish-language reel demonstrating five camera-motion keywords to type alongside an uploaded still in Google Flow: Dolly In for a smooth push toward the subject, Arc Left for a lateral orbit keeping the character centred, Overhead for a cinematic top-down angle, Crash Zoom for an aggressive snap-in, and a crane-up command for a rising shot. Each is shown applied to the same source image so the motion difference is visible. The post is a teaser for a PDF of 50+ such commands delivered by DM on comment, but the five demonstrated here are usable as-is.
items.author: luigivera.y

items.title: A fully automated French short: Claude Code writes it, HyperFrames renders it
items.synopsis: In a “pro ou mytho” verdict format, the creator reveals the short being shown features neither his face, his voice, his script, his edit nor his design work. The pipeline runs Claude Code from a terminal to write the video as code, HyperFrames to build it shot by shot, and a scheduler to publish weeks ahead — he notes he substituted HyperFrames for the more expensive tool in the technique he was copying. His verdict is that the workflow genuinely works.
items.author: jarod.le.cameleon

items.title: Italian comment-gated giveaway of an AI prompt pack
items.synopsis: A carousel post in Italian whose caption is purely a lead magnet: comment 'PROMPT' and the creator sends the complete pack for free. The visuals show AI-generated output but neither the model nor the prompts are named. The hashtags place it in the generic AI-creator trend space rather than describing any specific tool.
items.author: akapepinho

items.title: GPT-6 Astra plus free HyperFrames as a CapCut replacement for Reels
items.synopsis: The creator claims the reel itself was edited end to end by GPT-6 Astra — cuts, subtitles, motion design and sound effects — with no manual editing. The stack is two pieces: a paid ChatGPT plan (the €20 tier suffices) for Astra, which writes the animation as code, and the free HyperFrames tool, which renders that code into actual video. The caption adds the quota economics: Astra burns through a Plus quota fast in Codex, so the advice is to have Astra plan the edit and hand execution to the cheaper GPT-5.6 Sol.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: New camera angles from footage you already shot, using Krea and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The workflow starts by deciding which parts of an existing video must stay fixed and which shots or camera moves you want to add. The source video is then uploaded to Krea as a reference with Seedance 2.5 selected, and the prompt explicitly pins the constants — characters, actions, overall scene — while describing the new angles and movements. A few minutes later the same scene returns with different camera work, without regenerating the shot from scratch.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Higgsfield Genjutsu: motion transfer and selective object swap in video
items.synopsis: Genjutsu is presented as a control-first alternative to blanket AI video swap tools, offering two distinct modes. Motion transfer preserves the original movement, camera path and timing while replacing everything else; object swap changes only the element you select and leaves the rest of the frame untouched. The demonstrated workflow is deliberately short — open Genjutsu, pick a mode, upload your video plus references, hit generate — with the link gated behind a comment.
items.author: higgsfield.ai

items.title: Deux commandes Google Flow pour décliner une photo produit en publicités
items.synopsis: La démonstration part d'une seule image produit chargée dans Google Flow, puis utilise des commandes slash pour en tirer plusieurs formats publicitaires. La commande /UGC ad transforme l'image en publicité de style créateur et ajoute même un personnage cohérent avec le produit, tandis que /luxury ad produit une publicité cinématographique haut de gamme. L'auteur annonce plus de cinquante autres commandes produit du même type, envoyées en message privé à qui commente PRODUCT.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Generating a synthetic AI influencer through a Claude custom connector
items.synopsis: Hugo Matias opens by revealing the woman on screen is entirely AI-generated, then walks through reproducing her: copy an MCP server link, add it in the Claude settings as a custom connector, rename it and continue. A single prompt then returns a consistent AI influencer persona in about two minutes. The rest of the pitch is monetisation, posting the output to social platforms for reach and redirecting that traffic to a paid fan platform, with the full method gated behind a comment; the connector name is only spoken aloud, so the exact tool is not reliably identifiable from the video.
items.author: hugomatias.ai

items.title: Turning one talking-head take into an eight-camera studio shoot
items.synopsis: Nomada Toast demonstrates converting a single flat talking-head recording into footage that looks shot by a full studio camera rig. The workflow starts with a screenshot of the original take, runs it through an image generator to rebuild the scene as a professional studio, adding props with the pen tool or command-clicking to alter elements, then imports the original video alongside that still. Seedance 2.5 inside Lovart transforms the whole recording against the new reference, turning one shot into roughly eight distinct angles without reshooting.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Free open-source cinematic video generation with sound
items.synopsis: The creator dropped paid AI video subscriptions after finding a free open-source alternative. It generates cinematic video with sound effects from either text or images. Camera movement, effects, styles and scenes are controllable, and running it locally removes any cap on generations.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Open Art turns one sentence into a directed explainer video
items.synopsis: The whole demo video began from the single prompt “explain gravity”, with every subsequent refinement handled through conversation rather than a timeline. Testing it live on “explain recursion in a 30-second video”, the creator finds the tool generates a storyboard with GPT Image 2 and the audio track with Lyria, behind a paywall he ends up subscribing to. A second run explaining inflation in an anime style — which it chose to render in Spanish — also lands, and he rates it a “fact”.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Sell cinematic 3D restaurant menus made from one prompt
items.synopsis: The pitch is packaging AI-generated 3D menus as a premium digital product for restaurants. The workflow uploads photos of an existing menu to Google Flow, then pastes a single detailed prompt to produce the 3D effect. The output turns a flat menu into a cinematic animation with realistic detail and smooth transitions, ready to resell to multiple restaurants.
items.author: kushalfinds.ai

items.title: MiniMax H3 outputs 2K video with stereo audio in one pass
items.synopsis: China open-sourced MiniMax H3, an AI video model producing 2K video and stereo audio in a single pass. It combines video, speech, lip sync and music without stitching separate tools together. The licence permits commercial use.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Collage-style motion design with ChatGPT and Seedance
items.synopsis: A French walkthrough for producing collage-poster motion graphics using ChatGPT and Seedance 2.5. You first generate a still in ChatGPT describing the collage poster style, optionally importing a reference image to match, then ask ChatGPT to write a video prompt specifying that the animation starts on a blank canvas and reveals each collage element layer by layer. Pasting that prompt into Seedance with the reference image turns the still into a finished motion design animation.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Generate a new camera angle from a single image
items.synopsis: A French demo of an AI tool that converts any single image into a new camera angle in about thirty seconds. No editing software and no cost are involved. The creator uses it to fake convincing camera movement in video projects.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Drawing a drone path on a still image in Google Flow — rated hype
items.synopsis: The premise is appealing: open Google Flow, select the OmniFlash model, upload a photo, draw red lines tracing the path you want a drone to fly, then paste a set of instructions. The creator tries it on a hiking photo of himself and the output is poor, including the model altering his skin tone for no apparent reason. Three further attempts do not improve it, and he rates the feature hype.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Claude Code edits raw footage into DaVinci Resolve
items.synopsis: The creator hands raw video to Claude Code and gets a finished edit back in one click. The result lands directly in DaVinci Resolve ready to review. The pitch is removing both the editing subscription and the hired editor from the loop.
items.author: leon.petrou

items.title: MiniMax H3 run locally against Seedance 2.0
items.synopsis: A head-to-head comparison between a free AI video model and Seedance 2.0. The team runs MiniMax H3 locally on a Dell Precision T2 tower using prompts and reference images supplied by Higgsfield. The point is showing what a local workstation delivers versus a hosted commercial model.
items.author: badxstudio

items.title: Okay, the AI filmmaking suite, renders a Forrest Gump script page straight to screen
items.synopsis: The creator dropped a single unedited page of the Forrest Gump screenplay into Okay - the AI filmmaking suite now hosted at okaywannabe.com - selected Seedance 2.5 as the renderer and hit action with no further input. The output reproduced the scene's dialogue, character blocking and the stuck leg-brace beat directly from the script text alone. He notes the suite also exposes control over characters, cast and locations, covering writing, directing, casting, editing and composing in a single AI pipeline.
items.author: jmtasu

items.title: A paid Claude skill for cartoon commercials that failed six times — rated all hype
items.synopsis: The promised workflow was simple: find the repo on GitHub, ask Claude to install the skill, then point the R-CAD skill at your website to generate a cartoon-style commercial with research and planning handled for you. In practice the skill is paywalled, and after paying, the creator's generations failed roughly six times before producing one broken output with a laptop screen rendered on the wrong side. He puts the cost at $35 wasted and rates the tool all hype — a useful negative data point on paid Claude skills.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: A product ad from one image, storyboarded by AI
items.synopsis: A setup for producing a professional-looking product commercial with no ad budget. One product image is expanded into a nine-panel storyboard, then animated. The output is a finished ad ready to post.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Cutting social clips from three-hour podcasts
items.synopsis: Chat Video Pro is a plugin for extracting social clips from very long podcast recordings. It removes the subscription model, with each cut costing pennies. The creator frames it as a way for agencies to deliver more client value faster.
items.author: chatvideopro

items.title: Reviewing Claude Code video edits on a here.now page
items.synopsis: The creator edits entire videos with Claude Code, including motion graphics and captions, but found reviewing the cut miserable inside a chat window. Now Claude spins up a here.now page where the video can be watched and commented on at every timestamp needing a change. Claude then reads the feedback and builds the next version; here.now is made by Vercel and has its own agent integration.
items.author: mr.paidsocial

items.title: A full video from a single prompt with Seedance 2.5 on Morphic
items.synopsis: The creator made an entire video from one prompt using Seedance 2.5 inside Morphic Studios. The workflow is to open Morphic, select Seedance 2.5, add references, paste the prompt, and generate. The model supports 30-second single-shot videos, up to 50 references, and extending existing videos.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Three rules that keep AI video out of slop territory
items.synopsis: The creator argues the fastest route to AI slop is forcing one model to do every job, and instead maps tasks to models: Soul 2.0 for realism, Soul Cinema for cinematic frames, GPT 2.0 for text-heavy images, and Nano Banana 2.0 for general editing. Second, he says to prompt as if on set with an infinite budget — name the camera, the lens, the director whose eye you want, and the film the shot should feel like, because the real bottleneck is your film vocabulary rather than the tool. Third, add organic texture such as film grain, halation, and bloom, since AI output is too clean and lacks the sensor noise and lens imperfection a real camera introduces.
items.author: buck.the.aikami

items.title: AICameraControl poses a 3D model to lock the exact camera shot for AI images
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates using 3D models to obtain the exact shot and pose you want in AI images, starting at AICameraControl.com where you position the camera, move and rotate the model, add a second person, and adjust the pose down to individual body parts. Once the shot looks right you pick your image model, tick character sheet, and hit generate, which returns both the prompt and a reference frame to download. You then upload those into an image model such as Nano Banana Pro alongside your character sheet, and the generated image retains the pose and framing of the reference.
items.author: benkaluza.studio

items.title: yt-dlp downloads video from 1,700+ sites and pairs well with Claude
items.synopsis: The creator highlights yt-dlp as one of the most powerful and under-discussed GitHub repositories, with over 183,000 stars putting it in the top twenty repos worldwide. It downloads from more than 1,700 sites just from a URL — YouTube in 4K, whole playlists and channels in one command, Instagram reels and stories, TikTok, Facebook, X, Twitch, or audio only as MP3. It is public domain, needs no app, account, or AI credits, runs entirely locally, and can simply be handed to Claude.
items.author: alassafi.ai

items.title: Multi-angle edit from a single-camera take, via a Claude skill plus Google Omni
items.synopsis: The workflow chains two tools: a Claude skill transcribes the source video with precise timestamps and writes the entire downstream prompt automatically, then that prompt is pasted into Google Omni along with the original single-angle footage. Omni synthesises additional camera angles that were never filmed — the creator notes with some disbelief that it infers what the side of his head looks like. He flags one practical blocker, needing a VPN to Japan for access, and rates the tool a genuine “fact” rather than hype.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: The EU AI Act sanctions that went live on 2 August
items.synopsis: Since Sunday 2 August, part of the EU AI Act carries active sanctions, so an app shipping AI features may already be non-compliant. The creator poses three questions to determine whether you fall in scope. A companion document is offered for bringing an app into compliance if you do.
items.author: laforet.dev

items.title: Draw a path on an image and make the camera follow it
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates drawing directly on an image to define a path that the camera then follows through the generated shot. The technique is shown alongside a Higgsfield promotion offering Seedance 2.0 in 4K with two days of unlimited generation. A further seven days of unlimited Seedance 2.5 in 4K is announced for when that model lands on the platform.
items.author: jadheshvp

items.title: Italian AI prompt pack teased for comment delivery
items.synopsis: An Italian-language post offering a free complete prompt pack in exchange for a comment. The visible caption carries only trend hashtags and no description of the pack contents.
items.author: akapepinho

items.title: Wan2GP runs open-source AI video on a 6GB GPU
items.synopsis: Wan2GP is an open-source AI video generator built for people without cloud subscriptions or high-end hardware. It targets consumer GPUs, needing only about 6GB of VRAM to run. That puts it in reach of most mid-range NVIDIA cards from the past eight years.
items.author: karthikramaniai

items.title: Seven days of unlimited Higgsfield across Gemini OMNI Flash, Seedance 2.0 and Nano Banana Pro
items.synopsis: The creator promotes a one-day offer giving seven days of unlimited access to Higgsfield's top models. The visuals shown were made with Gemini OMNI Flash, but the plan also covers Seedance 2.0 and Nano Banana Pro. The offer advertises unlimited AI generation and unlimited cinematic video across all top models.
items.author: johngoldcreates

items.title: A Vox-style explainer built by one Claude Skill
items.synopsis: The creator produced an entire Vox-style explainer video from a single prompt using only Claude Code and Higgsfield. No script was written, no scene storyboarded and After Effects never opened. One Claude Skill handled research, voiceover and every on-screen visual, and the video walks the workflow step by step.
items.author: sanji.chien

items.title: Apple-style scroll-linked product animations in four no-code steps
items.synopsis: The creator reproduces the scroll-driven animations agencies charge thousands for — where a product spins or assembles itself as you scroll — in four steps with zero code. You generate a start frame and an end frame in Google Flow, use its frames-to-video mode to animate everything in between, then run that clip through EasyGIF's video-to-image-sequence tool at 30 frames per second and download the frames as a zip. Finally you drop the whole folder into your AI coding tool and ask it to build a scroll-linked image sequence on a canvas, which she notes is exactly the trick Apple uses on its product pages.
items.author: cindiezhu

items.title: Claude + Stitch for production-ready UI systems
items.synopsis: The post tackles Claude's historical weakness at frontend work by pairing it with Stitch, Google's UI generation tool. The workflow uses Stitch to generate full UI systems and then turns them into production-ready apps with animations and connected screens. The full setup and prompts are gated behind a 'Code' comment.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: UI/UX Pro Max Skill + 21st.dev Magic Chat for Claude
items.synopsis: This French video shows how to turn Claude into a professional UI/UX designer capable of generating very clean websites. The setup has two steps: install the UI/UX Pro Max Skill, then add Magic Chat from 21st.dev to access a huge library of interface components. The result is pro-level web design produced directly by the agent.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: Claude 'Carousel Maker' project for viral posts
items.synopsis: The post shows how to create viral Instagram carousels in under 60 seconds using Claude. You set up a dedicated 'Carousel Maker' project, paste the provided prompt, and Claude generates the slides, hooks, and content. The prompt itself is gated behind a 'Viral' comment.
items.author: lisaworldverse

items.title: A web-design tool that hands you the prompt, not just the page
items.synopsis: The creator presents a new web-coding tool that has taken the top spot for website design, generating clean professional layouts with modern gradients and fluid animations, entirely free. What impressed him is that it does not stop at the finished result — it also gives you the exact prompt used to create it. You take that prompt straight into Cursor or a similar builder and can modify the design instantly from there.
items.author: levibecodeur

items.title: Claude Code as a full website-design replacement
items.synopsis: A designer with 10+ years of experience claims Claude Code has replaced website designers, calling it the biggest shift he has seen. Work that used to cost thousands and take days now reportedly happens in seconds. He offers a stack guide for building high-quality websites with this AI workflow.
items.author: simon.saysai

items.title: An AI site builder generating immersive 3D scroll experiences from one prompt
items.synopsis: The creator positions this new AI website builder against Lovable, arguing that other vibe-coding tools produce clean but flat landing pages. This one instead generates a fully immersive 3D scroll-based site with real depth, real motion, and interactive elements that respond as you scroll. You describe the site in a single prompt and it builds the interactive 3D experience automatically.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: Ten mega-projects reshaping Athens, with budgets and dates
items.synopsis: The transcript turns a follow-prompt into a costed infrastructure rundown. Metro Line 4 is a wholly new 1.8 billion euro line of fifteen stations running from Alsos Veikou to Goudi, already well under construction, while two large football stadiums are advancing: Panathinaikos' ground in Votanikos has stands under construction targeting around 2027, and Olympiacos has unveiled a 250 million euro privately funded rebuild of Karaiskakis taking it from 33,000 to more than 53,000 seats, approved but not yet started pending permits. A 370 million euro coastal metropolitan park has just signed contracts with main construction from January 2027 and completion targeted for the second half of 2029, followed by a 380 million euro project in Marousi.
items.author: georgemoulosofficial

items.title: Cyprus Eats starts a European food-city series in Athens
items.synopsis: Episode one of a partnership series between @cypruseats and @seeyoutravelcy searching for Europe's best food cities, opening with Athens. The first three venues named are @lsandsia, @anthes.restaurant and @yphes.athens. The caption gates trip details behind a comment keyword.
items.author: cypruseats

items.title: Libertine, an Athens brunch for two at 28 euros with mimosas
items.synopsis: The transcript replaces a hashtag-only caption with a specific recommendation. Pamela, an American living in Greece, names Libertine as her absolute favourite brunch spot in Athens, calling it stylish, cosy and affordable with excellent food. The concrete detail is the bill: brunch for two including multiple mimosas came to just 28 euros.
items.author: thepamelaokyere

items.title: Kowalski, the Parisian-feeling Athens café tourists miss
items.synopsis: A detailed recommendation for Kowalskibar in Athens, which the creator says feels distinctly Parisian. It is framed as a jewel among Athens cafés that few tourists find, worth lingering in. The post is explicitly pitched as a save-for-later chic retreat from the busy city.
items.author: travelarias.official

items.title: Five historic Athens souvlaki spots, ranked, from 1924 onwards
items.synopsis: The transcript delivers the five venues in the creator's order of preference. It opens with Achilleas and his handmade gyros carrying nearly forty years of history, then the famous souvlaki of Kostas on Filellinon, whose bifteki they call the tastiest they have tried, from a recipe held since 1950. Christos in Egaleo has served pork kalamaki and handmade beef bifteki in fluffy oiled pita since 1988, followed by the first kebab shop in Greece, open since 1924, and a palm-sized souvlaki served strictly with onion, tomato, parsley and red pepper, running since 1951.
items.author: eatchers

items.title: Uncaptioned reel from an Athens makaronadiko
items.synopsis: A video from @akakiosmakaronadiko, a pasta-focused Greek eatery, posted with no caption text. The account name is the only clue to the subject. The content cannot be described further without the video.
items.author: akakiosmakaronadiko

items.title: Kowalski bar café, old-money elegance near Syntagma
items.synopsis: A reshared visit to Kowalskibar café in Athens, described as giving old-money vibes with elegant styling and good food. The caption gives walking times: ten minutes from Syntagma station or three from Panepistimio. It is saved as a central coffee destination.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: A zeibekiko performance that gives goosebumps
items.synopsis: A German-captioned clip of a zeibekiko, the solo Greek dance, which the creator says gave them goosebumps. There is no venue, event or performer named. It is cultural content rather than a travel tip.
items.author: diegriechen

items.title: The sacred ten souvlaki joints, opening with Achilleas in Neos Kosmos
items.synopsis: The transcript delivers the alphabetical ranking of the ten best souvlatzidika across Athens and Piraeus, with a recommended order at each. It opens in Neos Kosmos at Spintharou 18, where since March 1987 Achilleas has made what the creator calls the tastiest handmade gyros in Athens: preparation starts at 6am with meat from the Rentis meat market, the shop opens to the public at 4pm and the single daily gyros has physically run out by 7:30. It is seasoned with black pepper, oregano and a four-spice mix they blend themselves; the tour then drops down to the old market of Piraeus at Gounari 18.
items.author: ikon5

items.title: Souvlakination turns one, with a mission for souvlaki and gyros
items.synopsis: An anniversary post marking one year of Souvlakination, an account dedicated to souvlaki and gyros. The stated mission is to teach the world about souvlakia and gyros properly. The hashtags span both Athens and Thessaloniki gyradika.
items.author: souvlakination_

items.title: Athens' best restaurants in a five-creator carousel
items.synopsis: A carousel collecting restaurant and dish picks across Athens, crediting creators including @bouujiee, @snackeatingsnackss, @athen_food_explorer, @melbfoodieee and @eat.inathens. The caption asks readers to name their favourite traditional dish. Specific venues appear on the slides rather than in the text.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: An ultimate Athens guide in five creator slides
items.synopsis: A five-slide Athens guide compiled from five different travel creators. The caption is engagement-led, nudging readers to tag a friend who owes them a trip. It serves as general destination inspiration.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Three days in Athens: history, culture and endless souvlaki
items.synopsis: A condensed three-day Athens trip report reshared from @threedaytravels. It frames the city as a mix of historical sites, cultural stops and constant souvlaki. No individual venues are named in the caption.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Foinikas, Mexican food and cocktails in Athens
items.synopsis: A venue post from Foinikas Cocina Mexicana promoting its summer season as the Mexico of the city. The offer spans Mexican cocktails, tacos and burritos. A reservation phone number and DM booking are given in the caption.
items.author: foinikas_cocina_mexicana_

items.title: A six-slide Athens guide from ancient sites to neighbourhoods
items.synopsis: A carousel assembling six creators' views of Athens, moving from archaeological landmarks to the city's distinct neighbourhoods. Each slide carries its own photo credit. It is a broad orientation guide rather than a venue list.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Three hidden Greek street-food counters, with full addresses
items.synopsis: Athens Food on Foot names three lesser-known street-food stops with street addresses: Souvlaki Livadia at Kaniggos 2-4, the kantina at Karageorgi and Servias 2, and Ta mpifteakakia Karagiannis at 67a of the Varvakios Central Market. The post doubles as promotion for the operator's walking food tours. The addresses make it the most actionable street-food save in the set.
items.author: athens_foodonfoot

items.title: Baba au Rum, Athens cocktail institution
items.synopsis: A reshared visit to Baba au Rum in Athens, focused on its cocktail programme and evening atmosphere. The clip is credited to @greekality. It is saved as a drinks destination rather than a dining one.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: The Roosters, a new three-floor Athens coffee and brunch spot
items.synopsis: A first look at The Roosters in Athens, a newly opened venue the creator expects to become a personal favourite. The draw is three airy designed floors plus sun terraces, suited to coffee, brunch or just lingering. It is pitched as a meet-your-friends all-day space.
items.author: athen_food_explorer

items.title: Maria Callas Museum plus two bakeries, with an Acropolis view
items.synopsis: A three-stop central Athens walk that pairs the Maria Callas Museum with the 72h Artisanal Bakery and Ergon Bakehouse. The creator stumbled on the museum en route to the bakery and rates all three as must-visits. One of the stops also offers an Acropolis view.
items.author: thelenivee

items.title: Lunu Athens, a brunch and coffee favourite
items.synopsis: Athens Food List declares itself in love with Lunu Athens, with hashtags pointing to brunch, coffee, pancakes and burgers. The caption carries no address or dish detail. It is a single-venue brunch bookmark.
items.author: athens.foodlist

items.title: A gastronomic adventure through Athens
items.synopsis: A reshared Athens food tour following @linhforthehuynh through a series of traditional dishes. The caption asks viewers to name their favourite Greek dish rather than listing the venues shown. It is engagement-led food inspiration.
items.author: greece.explores

items.title: Five Athens wrap counters, from Elliniko to Drapetsona
items.synopsis: The transcript turns a one-line caption into a five-stop wrap tour. It starts with the famous souvlaki of Elliniko, where the queue is the tell, then stays in the southern suburbs for Mani Mani in Argyroupoli, which puts gourounopoula, slow-roast pork, inside the wrap. Patisia contributes Vasiliki, a traditional pita shop with wraps the audience recommended, Drapetsona hides one with fluffy pita, juicy meat and an aromatic sauce, and the tour closes with a souvlaki carrying nearly fifty years of tradition, served without potatoes but with a very good tomato sauce.
items.author: eatchers

items.title: Papalina in Petralona, Greek seafood
items.synopsis: A location-pin post for Papalina in the Petralona district of Athens. The hashtags place it squarely in Greek seafood and Greek cuisine. The caption itself is just the pin, so the visuals carry the detail.
items.author: pau_alexiou
