items.title: Convoi, an Athens burger pick from Athens Food List
items.synopsis: A near-wordless endorsement of Convoi, tagged by Athens Food List with burger and food hashtags. No dish detail or address appears in the caption. It is a one-venue bookmark.
items.author: athens.foodlist

items.title: Five of the best Athens stops in one carousel
items.synopsis: A five-slide carousel collecting creator picks across Athens: Tylixto Greek Wrap, Smyrni Baklava, Ohh Boy, a general Athens slide and Little Kook. Each slide credits a different creator. The named venues span wraps, sweets and themed cafés.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: The Syntagma kantina with a view over spring in Athens
items.synopsis: A Greek-language tip for the kantina on Karageorgi Servias near Syntagma Square, pitched as a shared local secret. The draw is experiencing spring in Athens from above. The post invites readers to tag the account when they visit.
items.author: foodnmoodgr

items.title: Plaka in the Athens light
items.synopsis: A scenic reel of the Plaka district reshared with a photographer credit by Greece Whispers. It is visual atmosphere with no venue or practical detail. Saved as neighbourhood inspiration.
items.author: greecewhispers

items.title: Roasting Warehouse, Australian-style single-origin coffee and brunch
items.synopsis: A Greek-language review of Roasting Warehouse, described as the city's talk-of-the-town opening. It serves selected single-origin coffees from Australian blends roasted in an on-site laboratory, with an Australian-leaning all-day brunch menu. The reviewer highlights a green outlook and a feel-good atmosphere.
items.author: athens.foodlist

items.title: A three-day Athens itinerary with eleven named sites
items.synopsis: A full three-day Athens itinerary credited to @threedaytravels, listing Monastiraki Square, the Ancient Agora, Metropolis Cathedral, the National Garden, the Panathenaic Stadium, the Acropolis, the Theatre of Dionysus, the Acropolis Museum, the Temple of Olympian Zeus, the National Archaeological Museum and Mount Lycabettus. The sequencing is the product. It is the most directly usable planning asset in this batch.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Eat in Athens' current favourite brunch spots
items.synopsis: A brunch roundup of the venues Eat in Athens has been returning to, built around eggs and coffee. The caption poses a pick-one question to the audience rather than listing addresses. Venue identification depends on the visuals.
items.author: eatin.athens

items.title: Neropistolo, a new French-influenced bakery on Voulis Street
items.synopsis: A visit to Neropistolo, a newly opened bakery and patisserie on Voulis Street in central Athens. The concept is a fusion of French pastry technique with local products. The reviewer visited with @madamegateauxathens and frames it as unmissable for carb and sugar lovers.
items.author: athen_food_explorer

items.title: Choureal, made-to-order profiteroles and éclairs on Ermou
items.synopsis: A review of Choureal, a multi-award-winning Athens patisserie where profiteroles, choux and éclairs are built to order. Customers choose dark, white or milk chocolate or caramel plus toppings such as biscuit, almonds or Oreos. The address given is Ermou 18 and Diomeias 2 in Syntagma.
items.author: theboyvoyage

items.title: Greek City Times endorses Mantri Athens for lamb and sheep
items.synopsis: Greek City Times reshares a recommendation for Mantri in the Athens foothills, adding their own endorsement. The kitchen specialises in elevated Greek dishes built around sheep and lamb, in a cosy modern room. Readers are advised to reserve.
items.author: greekcitytimes

items.title: Butterfly all day bar's new menu by chef Giorgos Tsoulis
items.synopsis: Athens Food List flags a new menu at Butterfly all day bar, created by chef Giorgos Tsoulis. The visuals lean on pancakes and brunch plates. It is a menu-change alert for an existing venue rather than a new opening.

items.title: Four Athens street-food stops you should not miss
items.synopsis: A named street-food shortlist for Athens: Smak, Pax Burgeristas, Zisis Fish in the Cone and Lukumades. The clip is credited to @taylorrrwalker. The explicit venue names make it directly actionable.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Counting down to the Greek summer
items.synopsis: A reshared scenic clip building anticipation for Greece's summer season, credited to @kalli_kati. It names no destination or venue. It functions as seasonal destination inspiration only.
items.author: greece.explores

items.title: Bubble dinner on the Neoma Hotel rooftop with an Acropolis view
items.synopsis: A write-up of the winter bubble-dining experience on the rooftop of the Neoma Hotel in Athens, where diners eat inside a transparent dome. The creator notes a free Acropolis view and says prices are reasonable. The experience is bookable during the winter months.
items.author: tzatchickie

items.title: oZe Athens in Zografou, croissants and tsoureki-dough pastries
items.synopsis: A Greek-language review of oZe, a new arrival on Papagou Street in the Zografou district of Athens. The concept is croissants and products built on tsoureki dough, in both savoury and sweet versions. The reviewer singles out the handmade mushroom pie and a strawberry-and-cream Tsoureki Bun.
items.author: foooodiesgr

items.title: Netflix's One Day drives a 32 percent Airbnb booking spike on a Greek island
items.synopsis: Greek Reporter covers a thirty-two percent rise in Airbnb bookings to a Greek island following the release of the Netflix series One Day, which filmed in Greece alongside Rome, London and Edinburgh. The story is about screen-tourism demand rather than travel advice. It is a market-trend data point.
items.author: greekreporter

items.title: Picky Coffee Roasters and Brunch, an Athens hidden gem
items.synopsis: A reshared visit to Picky Coffee Roasters and Brunch in Athens, framed as one of the city's lesser-known finds. The draw is coffee alongside a brunch menu. It is a single-venue coffee and brunch save.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: An unmarked Athens restaurant worth going back to twice
items.synopsis: The transcript reveals an unmarked restaurant in Athens where the creator had one of the best meals of their life, complete with a resident cat and a room so busy they sat inside. The dishes were free bread, roasted beets with goat cheese over the beet greens most Americans discard, fava made from yellow split peas under heavy olive oil, standout potatoes, Greek finger food and mushrooms in olive oil. The meal was good enough that they returned a second time to check they were not imagining it, staying for local ouzo and a homely dessert; the venue is deliberately never named.
items.author: joshetcetera

items.title: To Yiasemi, an Athens meat spot for black angus and pancetta
items.synopsis: A short recommendation for To Yiasemi, filed by Athens Food List as a must-visit meat venue. The highlighted items are black angus and pancetta. The caption is brief, with the hashtags carrying most of the context.
items.author: athens.foodlist

items.title: Wandering the alleys of Plaka
items.synopsis: A walking reel through Plaka, the old quarter beneath the Acropolis, reshared from @christinatouloumtzidou. The focus is the character of the narrow streets. No venues are named, so it serves as neighbourhood orientation.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: The Acropolis of Athens in a single reel
items.synopsis: A scenic clip of the Acropolis reshared from @alexandradts, framed around the scale of the monument. It carries no visiting logistics such as tickets or timing. Pure landmark inspiration.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Pax Burgers, an Athens burger stop
items.synopsis: A short burger-focused clip pointing to Pax Burgers in Athens, credited to @eat.inathens. The pitch is the build and bite of the burger itself. It is a single-venue save for casual eating.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Athens' hidden history, corner by corner
items.synopsis: A city montage reshared from @beccabillis presenting Athens as a place where history surfaces at every turn. It is atmosphere and sightseeing rather than a named-venue guide. Useful as general pre-trip inspiration.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Free things to do in Athens, from ruins to street art
items.synopsis: A roundup of no-cost Athens experiences, spanning ancient ruins and the city's street-art scene, credited to @greekality. The angle is seeing the city without an admission fee. Individual locations are shown visually rather than listed in the caption.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: An Athens food crawl from gyros to baklava
items.synopsis: A reshared food tour of Athens moving from gyro stands to baklava counters, credited to @angels_travels. Each dish is framed as carrying a piece of culinary tradition. The caption names no addresses, so the value is visual shortlisting.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Athens as history, cuisine and ancient streets in one reel
items.synopsis: A general Athens travel montage reshared from @pursesandplanes, mixing archaeological sites, food and street wandering. No specific venues or addresses are named. It is broad destination inspiration rather than an actionable tip.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Astypalaia, the butterfly-shaped Greek island
items.synopsis: A scenic reel of Astypalaia island shared by Greek Reporter with a photographer credit. It is pure island scenery with no itinerary or venue information. Saved under Athens, it functions as wider Greece travel inspiration.
items.author: greekreporter

items.title: Orizontes Lycabettus, dining with panoramic Athens views
items.synopsis: A clip promoting Orizontes Lycabettus, where the draw is a panoramic view over Athens from the hill alongside the food. The creator frames each dish as paired with the vista. It is filed as a special-occasion view restaurant.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Mantri Athens, an elevated Greek sheep and lamb specialist
items.synopsis: A visit to Mantri in the foothills of Athens, presented as a semi-secret spot in a cosy modern setting. The kitchen's speciality is sheep and lamb in elevated Greek preparations. The creator advises booking ahead, particularly for golden hour.
items.author: katkalkas

items.title: Three secret Athens restaurants, including a 95-year family tavern
items.synopsis: A three-name list of lesser-known Athens restaurants: Diporto for local food, Avli in Psiri as a locals' spot, and Taverna Klimataria, family-run for ninety-five years. The framing is deliberately anti-tourist-trap. The named venues are the takeaway.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Acera breakfast in Kallithea, with address and booking line
items.synopsis: A venue post for Acera in Kallithea, pitched on generous all-day breakfast and brunch portions. The caption carries the practical details: Mantzagriotaki 105 and a phone number for reservations. It reads as a neighbourhood brunch option away from the tourist centre.
items.author: zyme_kallithea

items.title: Tazza all day bistro, an aesthetic Athens lunch spot
items.synopsis: A reshared clip highlighting Tazza all day bistro in Athens as a design-led lunch venue. The emphasis is on the look of the room and the plating rather than a menu breakdown. It is saved as an atmosphere-first lunch option.
items.author: athenstravel

items.title: Five Athens brunch spots with smoothies and good coffee
items.synopsis: A named brunch shortlist spanning central Athens and the coast: Wanna Flirt, High Five Brunch, Qahwa in Egaleo, Boho Sea Life at Marina Flisvos and Sofi's Eatery in Vouliagmeni. The pitch is avocado-led brunch plates with smoothies and coffee. The geographic spread makes it useful beyond the city centre.
items.author: eatin.athens

items.title: Christos Lentzos, the inventor of the Greek frappé, dies at 93
items.synopsis: Greek Reporter marks the death at 93 of Christos Lentzos, credited as the mastermind behind the frappé. The piece traces his legacy to a café in the Pagrati neighbourhood of Athens and frames it as the end of an era in Greek coffee culture. It is a cultural-history note rather than a venue recommendation.
items.author: greekreporter

items.title: Brown Hotels' retro design hotel in central Athens
items.synopsis: A brand post from Brown Hotels promoting a retro-design property in the centre of Athens. The selling points are upscale service, a central location and a rooftop bar and restaurant. It is accommodation research rather than a food or sightseeing tip.

items.title: To Treno sto Rouf, the Athens restaurant inside a train
items.synopsis: A showcase of To Treno sto Rouf, an Athens restaurant set inside railway carriages, shared as a photography credit post. The appeal is the converted-train dining room rather than a specific dish. It is filed as a visually distinctive dinner venue.

items.title: Six traditional Greek restaurants in Athens, named
items.synopsis: A named shortlist of six traditional Athens restaurants: Karamanlidika, Atlantikos, Taverna Klimataria, Avli, Lolos and Tis theatrou to steki. The creators pitch it from a digital-nomad and work-from-Greece angle. Its value is the explicit list of venues rather than any single review.

items.synopsis: A five-stop café roundup for Athens, credited to @greekality and reshared by the Athens Travel account. The focus is on where to find the finest brews in the city. It is a save-for-later coffee shortlist rather than a detailed tasting note.

items.synopsis: A visit to Klimataria, a Greek tavern over a hundred years old that the creator calls a culinary time capsule. The post sells the place as history and gastronomy in one sitting rather than a modern restaurant experience.

items.synopsis: A rapid-fire Athens eating tour covering authentic Greek yogurt, a spinach and feta croissant, Greek-style pizza and a souvlaki counter the creator says ranks among the 150 best restaurants in the world. items.title: Neutralising coloured under-eye circles before concealer
items.synopsis: A French makeup tutorial showing how to colour-correct pigmented under-eye circles rather than burying them in concealer. The promised result is a de-tired look with far less product. It is a technique tip, not a product review.

items.synopsis: A French-language reel promoting Mina, a restaurant on Chaussée d'Ixelles in Brussels, built around Italian-inspired cooking, a cocktail list and a warm evening atmosphere. The clip is pure venue ambience — plated dishes, drinks being poured and interior shots — rather than a review or a menu breakdown. Beyond the street location no prices, opening hours or booking details are given.

items.synopsis: A short recommendation of Nami Handrolls in Brussels as the perfect spot for a date night or dinner with friends. The caption gives the venue tag and the occasion. No dishes or prices are listed.

items.title: A speakeasy cocktail served with a rose in the glass
items.synopsis: A French review of a venue the creator says is no longer new but remains genuinely unique, with a speakeasy feel, subdued lighting and a beautiful room. The evening opened with a cocktail called L'Heure du Loup served with a rose in the glass, which they rate divine. On the food side they had crisp croquetas and a very fresh ceviche, from a menu offering sharing plates; the caption does not name the venue.
items.author: sarahmirana

items.title: Free mochi at Wanli in Anderlecht for showing the video
items.synopsis: A deal post for Wanli Brussels at Rue de l'Agrafe 53 in 1070 Anderlecht, a short walk from Aumale metro station. Showing the video earns a free pack of mochi with a minimum ten-euro purchase, valid at the Anderlecht address only. The creator notes a second, smaller store in the centre opposite Brucity, and gives the Anderlecht weekday opening hours.

items.title: Five hidden Brussels gems, part three
items.synopsis: The third instalment of the hidden-gems series: Lila 29 for an incredible view and setting for drinks or dinner, Maison Louise as a hidden and very elegant restaurant with a garden that comes into its own with the first sun, Dolce Campana for authentic Italian cooking in a dimly lit room suited to a romantic dinner, and Brol. Each entry gets a one-line characterisation. It extends the same named-venue format.

items.title: Five hidden Brussels gems, part two
items.synopsis: The second instalment of a hidden-gems series, naming Big Cake for lunch, coffee or working in a beautiful setting, Tope Brussels as a rooftop with a striking city view, Corinthia for a chic timeless moment with top service, and Café Léopold for a cosy drink or something sweet. The creator closes with a secret spot they rate as the best fluffy pancakes. The named venues are the takeaway.
items.author: sarahmirana

items.title: Sina Pasta Bar moves to Rue des Bouchers, same recipes
items.synopsis: A relocation announcement from Sina Pasta Bar, now at 36 Rue des Bouchers in 1000 Brussels, stressing that the recipes are unchanged. The caption quotes a claim that it is the best Italian in Brussels. It is a move notice rather than a new opening.
items.author: sina.pasta.bar

items.title: Brussels Sauna opening promotion
items.synopsis: A short French post from Brussels Sauna inviting bookings and pointing to an opening promotion. Neither the discount, the dates nor the address is specified. The caption establishes only that the venue has newly opened.
items.author: brusselssauna

items.title: Four gems in the north of Brussels, from a resident
items.synopsis: A French roundup from a creator who lives in northern Brussels and finds the area short on options. Brol is a very cosy brunch spot with incredible homemade pastries and mushroom toasts they recommend without reservation. Nine Coffee in Wemmel is the new ultra-aesthetic address for matcha.
items.author: sarahmirana

items.title: L'Improbable, a hidden Ixelles terrace with seasonal cooking
items.synopsis: A disclosed paid collaboration covering L'Improbable in Ixelles, sought out for its concealed terrace. The creator found more than that: a warm welcome from Alexandra front of house and Mathieu's seasonal cooking, with plates they describe as precisely judged. The standout note is the rare sensation of being outside the city while still in the middle of Brussels.
items.author: gourmettes_bavardes

items.title: Porte de Namur, from medieval gate to Brusselization
items.synopsis: A history explainer on Porte de Namur, once one of the great medieval gates of Brussels where merchants, soldiers and travellers entered from the Namur road. The fortified gate disappeared in the late 1700s, replaced by toll pavilions, fountains, trams and Belle Époque mansions that made it a fashionable entrance by the 1900s. The account then turns to the postwar demolition wave known as Brusselization.
items.author: travelreinhard

items.title: The Hooikaai, Brussels' 17th-century Hay Wharf
items.synopsis: A local-history explainer on the Hooikaai, once part of Brussels' old inner harbour and directly connected to the River Zenne and the canal network that carried trade into the city. The dock was dug in the seventeenth century during the expansion of the Port of Brussels, and for centuries ships unloaded here in one of the busiest commercial districts. The name translates as Hay Wharf.
items.author: travelreinhard

items.title: Victor Horta's Maison du Peuple, his most ambitious project
items.synopsis: An architecture explainer on Victor Horta, the Belgian architect who lived from 1861 to 1947 and pioneered Art Nouveau through innovative use of iron, glass and flowing natural forms. Several of his Brussels buildings are now UNESCO World Heritage Sites. The focus is the Maison du Peuple, one of his most ambitious projects and a departure from his luxurious private townhouses.
items.author: travelreinhard

items.title: Poncho in Waterloo, cocktails on the terrace
items.synopsis: A short French post from an invited visit to Poncho in Waterloo, where the creator says the food was extremely good. The hashtags point to the terrace as the draw. No dishes or prices are specified.
items.author: margaux.marissen

items.title: Opening dates for eight Brussels summer terraces and rooftops
items.synopsis: A dated calendar of summer hotspot openings in Brussels: Casa Alta on 1 April, La Guinguette at Serra Brussels on 23 April, the ninth floor at 58.bxl on 28 April, Jeux d'été Brussels and Soko Rooftop both on 30 April, Le Jardin du Lily's Tulum Edition on 13 May, La Terrasse 02 on 14 May and The Roof by The1040 on 28 May. The creator notes most clips are from last year except the two already open. It is a planning calendar rather than a review.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: The viral Brussels cinnamon roll place, taste-tested next to the Grand-Place
items.synopsis: The creator goes to the newly opened cinnamon roll shop she had seen all over social media, located right beside the Grand-Place in Brussels, and orders blueberry for herself, pistachio for her friend, plus a matcha on the strength of its reputation. Her verdict is positive on all counts: prices she considers fair for a large roll in that location, the pistachio cream better than her own choice, and a matcha with the deep green colour she wanted. She says she will go back — but neither caption nor audio ever names the shop, so the address has to be read off the video.
items.author: julieverven

items.title: Buga Ramen's own pitch: halal and vegan Japanese on Rue de la Fourche
items.synopsis: A venue post from Buga Ramen on Rue de la Fourche in Brussels, selling itself as Tokyo in Brussels with every bowl evoking Akihabara. The menu covers ramen, crisp karaage and soft bao, with halal and vegan options so nobody is excluded. Dine-in or delivery both feed a loyalty card that ends in a figurine.
items.author: bugaramenbxl

items.title: Comer Actual Tacos brings Mexico to Saint-Gilles
items.synopsis: A French review of Comer Actual Tacos in Saint-Gilles, run by a team the creator says masters the taco like no one else. The tortillas are made in house and the flavours described as exploding in the mouth. They pair it with a fresh bissap.
items.author: bruxelles_secrete_

items.title: Julien Othomene brings Parisian haute pâtisserie to Ixelles
items.synopsis: A French feature on a patisserie conceived by Julien Othomene, a pastry chef with a haute-gastronomy background who set out to import the craft of the great Parisian houses into the heart of Ixelles. The range runs from an ultra-creamy chocolate flan to a signature Saint-Honoré the creator calls a genuine favourite. Each creation is framed as a lesson in balance.
items.author: bruxelles_secrete_

items.title: Eight Brussels restaurants tagged in one roundup
items.synopsis: A French post whose value is the tag list: La Fabbrica at Tour & Taxis, 58.bxl, Corinthia Brussels, Lily's Brussels, Nami Handrolls, Bortier BXL, Big Mamma Belgium and Lila29. No individual reviews or addresses are given. It functions as a shortlist of the city's current hotspots.
items.author: unpeudelou

items.title: So Soir on RATZ: a 3,500 square metre food market in a converted garage
items.synopsis: A magazine feature on RATZ, a newly opened food market of three thousand five hundred square metres on Place Saint-Boniface in Ixelles, at Rue Saint-Boniface 25 in 1050. The site is a garage wholly transformed into an immersive world drawing on Asia and the Middle East. There are fourteen culinary counters, but the writers say the decor is the main reason to go.
items.author: sosoirmagazine

items.title: RATZ, a new 3,000 square metre food court at Saint-Boniface
items.synopsis: An announcement of RATZ, a new Brussels food court on Place Saint-Boniface. It spans three thousand square metres over several floors with fourteen stands serving cuisines from around the world. The creator flags it as a place worth saving.
items.author: davidantoine

items.title: Magasin Panda goes retail: Rituals-style 500ml bottles at 3.50 euros
items.synopsis: The transcript reveals the Saturday appointment as the retail launch of Magasin Panda at Chaussée de Mons 1425, opposite the IKEA in Anderlecht with a KFC alongside, on 14 February at 10am. The shop has just moved to one hundred percent retail, meaning no minimum order and no minimum spend, so customers can buy a single item. The headline comparison is private-collection fragrances the creator says cost 40 euros at Rituals selling for 3.50 in 500ml, across sakura, lotus flower and oud variants, alongside a three-litre, sixty-wash Panda laundry detergent at three euros.
items.author: soufyane_derdour

items.title: Le Thème, a festive Brussels restaurant with a darbouka show
items.synopsis: A French review of Le Thème in Brussels, visited as a festive night out. The food is rated very good, with the pavlova and a revisited Dubai-style dessert singled out, and the atmosphere carries a live darbouka performance. The creator notes it is halal with the exception of the beef sirloin carpaccio, and recommends it for birthdays or a night with friends.
items.author: iam_.nyia

items.title: Challenge Lab, a 55-minute group experience with a discount code
items.synopsis: A disclosed advertising post for Challenge Lab Experience at Rue de l'Ecuyer 63/65 in 1000 Brussels, suitable for groups of two to six and pitched as a date-night idea. Tickets are booked through the Fever app at around 25 euros per person depending on the date, with code CHALLENGEGUIDE10 giving ten percent off. Each session runs 55 to 60 minutes.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Tsuki closes its winter bubbles and opens its Japanese garden for summer
items.synopsis: A seasonal update from Tsuki Brussels announcing that its winter dining bubbles are closing for the summer after a season of bookings, dinners and birthdays. The bubbles will return with the first cold weather. In the meantime the Japanese garden terrace is open all summer with no reservation required.
items.author: tsuki_brussels

items.title: The best pancakes at La Graine Coffee on Chaussée de Gand
items.synopsis: A disclosed gifted post in which the creator says they ate the best pancakes at La Graine Coffee. The hashtags place it on the Chaussée de Gand in Brussels. Beyond the pancake verdict the caption carries no menu or pricing detail.
items.author: studentspot_light

items.title: Three Mexican addresses in Brussels, with the dishes named
items.synopsis: A French three-stop Mexican roundup. Gringo at Châtelain offers a retro room, fresh produce and house sauces, with the creator's favourite being green tomato, avocado, lime and chilli, plus revisited tacos and a cheesy pulled-beef Gringa. Ancho at Louise follows with chicken-and-lime quesadillas, a trio of tacos the creator calls incredible and very generous burritos.
items.author: foodctrl.bx

items.title: Buga Ramen, a Tokyo moment on Rue de la Fourche
items.synopsis: A review of Buga Ramen at Rue de la Fourche 9 in 1000 Brussels, pitched as the next best thing to going to Japan. The creator rates the food decent but says the decor steals the show, making it worth visiting for the experience. Vegetarian options are available.
items.author: loanergy

items.title: Frites Atelier, fries designed by a three-star chef

items.title: Sunny Bao, under-10-euro East Asian street food in Ixelles

Seating is limited with a small outside terrace, so it works mainly as takeaway, with halal, pescatarian and vegetarian options.

The space is large and bright with both indoor and outdoor areas, and the creator rates it ideal for sunset. The menu covers Iberian-inspired finger food and sharing plates.
items.author: thetinynomad

items.title: Pepe's beeswax ice cream voted the best in Belgium
items.synopsis: A French feature on Pepe's Glacier, which took the prize for best ice cream in Belgium in February after months of work. The winning flavour was a beeswax ice cream, described as a rich, original and refreshing creation. It came out of Pepe's artisanal practice in collaboration with another craftsman, Hafid Jouhri.
items.author: zoe_stene

items.title: El Cielo, a Wednesday latino rooftop on the Bozar terrace
items.synopsis: A French feature on El Cielo Rooftop, running every Wednesday from 16:00 to 22:30 on the Bozar rooftop in central Brussels. The programme is latino music covering reggaeton, salsa and bachata, with cocktails including XL mojitos and food such as empanadas and nachos, plus a city view. An afterparty follows at La Clave Latinos Club.
items.author: isavidalocaa

items.title: Öken, a dimly lit speakeasy with carefully built cocktails
items.synopsis: A French recommendation for Öken Brussels, a bar the creator discovered months earlier and felt obliged to share. They describe it as a departure from what Brussels usually offers, with subdued lighting and highly worked cocktails. It is pitched for drinks with friends or a partner.
items.author: odavintage

items.title: Cove, a new aesthetic brunch spot in Brussels
items.synopsis: A short announcement of Cove Brussels as the city's new design-led brunch address, tagged with pancake and matcha cues. The hashtags mark it halal and position it as a hidden-gem dessert and brunch venue. No address or pricing is given in the caption.
items.author: little.brussels

items.title: Emilia in Waterloo, Bologna cooking with the full price list
items.synopsis: A disclosed paid collaboration covering Emilia at Rue de la Station 29 in 1410 Waterloo, serving real Bologna flavours built on parmesan, fresh pasta and balsamic vinegar. Pricing is itemised: a 35-euro lunch menu of starter, pasta and dessert, a six-course set menu at 75 euros, pasta fresca at 22 to 24 and secondi at 22 to 32. The creator states the address was validated before committing.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: La Pizza è Bella in Antwerp, rated five stars for about 40 euros
items.synopsis: A structured review of La Pizza è Bella at Oever 2 in 2000 Antwerp, scored five out of five at roughly 40 euros. The creator describes a genuinely Italian experience with a warm welcome and highlights the starter in particular. Note the venue is in Antwerp despite the post being filed under Brussels.
items.author: foodantwerp

items.title: Brasserie Boemvol on place de la Bourse still seats you at 9pm
items.synopsis: A French review of Brasserie Boemvol, a brand-new Belgian brasserie on place de la Bourse in central Brussels. The creator's point of praise is being seated immediately at 21:00, which they note is genuinely hard in Belgium. They ordered a single main and rate the dish good.
items.author: odavintage

items.title: Two Brussels burger spots united by Pauwels sauces
items.synopsis: A French double feature on two central Brussels venues that share a sauce supplier, Pauwels Sauces. The first is HKS BXL at 122 Rue de Flandre, a burger bar where you build the burger from scratch. The creator's build used a pesto bun with Pauwels aioli for a Provençal note, plus steak, gouda and grilled vegetables.
items.author: labazeee

items.title: Five favourite halal brunch spots in Brussels, named
items.synopsis: A bilingual top-five of halal brunch venues in Brussels, presented in no particular order: Baba Brussels, La Table Rustique, Cliff Brussels, Brol Coffee House and Caffe Batavia. Each is tagged with a food emoji hinting at its speciality. The explicit naming makes it directly actionable.
items.author: brusselshalalfood

items.title: Le Jardin du Lily's, a hidden terrace between Louise and La Cambre
items.synopsis: A French look at Le Jardin du Lily's, a newly opened terrace tucked between avenue Louise and the Abbaye de la Cambre. The setting is planted and elegant with deckchairs on the grass, vintage-style furniture, a DJ in the background and string lights. Signature cocktails such as the Lily's Candy are joined by small plates to pick at.
items.author: _lanaomi

items.title: Casa Alta, an Ibiza-flavoured rooftop open daily until 1am
items.synopsis: A French feature on Casa Alta BXL, a rooftop in the heart of Brussels pitched with Ibiza vibes. It offers an original drinks list, an unobstructed view over the city, sun spots and cosier corners furnished with vintage finds. It opens every day from 17:00 to 1:00.
items.author: odavintage

items.title: Lila29 opens on the 29th floor of The Standard, Iberian-inspired
items.synopsis: The opening of Lila29 on the twenty-ninth floor of the new Standard Brussels hotel at Bd Roi Albert II 30 in 1000 Brussels. The menu is Iberian-inspired by chef Alex Joseph, available for cocktails only or full dinner, with bookings strongly advised. Lunch runs Thursday to Saturday from 12:00 to 3pm, with afterwork and dinner Tuesday to Saturday.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Grande Piazza called the best Italian in Brussels
items.synopsis: A short endorsement from Brussels Girlies declaring Grande Piazza the best Italian restaurant in Brussels and urging readers to go. The caption is enthusiasm plus the tag, with no dish or price detail. It corroborates the other Grande Piazza coverage in this folder.
items.author: brussels.girlies

items.title: A newly opened all-day café in the Sablon with a tree-shaded courtyard
items.synopsis: A French first look at a café that has just opened in the heart of the Sablon quarter in central Brussels, which the creator expects to become a favourite. The space is large and includes a pretty tree-planted courtyard that escapes the city noise. It serves coffee, breakfast, lunch and dinner; the caption does not give the venue's name.
items.author: thetinynomad

items.title: Tartlets, trompe-l'oeil pastries and cookies
items.synopsis: A disclosed gifted post praising tartlets, trompe-l'oeil pastries and cookies as very good. The venue is not named in the caption. Only the pastry categories can be identified from the text.
items.author: brussels_foodspots

items.title: A build-your-own soup spot on Rue E. Solvay, with an allergy warning
items.synopsis: A French recommendation for a soup venue at Rue E. Solvay 6 in 1050 Ixelles that the creator is still dreaming about. They recommend it to anyone who likes this style of soup. They add a clear caveat: despite each diner having their own tongs, the ingredients sit close together, so they would advise against it for anyone with significant allergies.
items.author: suchagirl

items.title: New Philly cheesesteaks in Brussels
items.synopsis: A short post announcing a new arrival the creator already calls iconic, serving Philly cheesesteaks described as juicy and cheesy. The hashtags mark it as a halal Brussels spot. No venue name, address or price appears in the caption.
items.author: little.brussels

items.title: A 29.50-euro halal Mediterranean brunch with four dated sittings
items.synopsis: A brunch announcement giving the next four dates as 11 May, 25 May, 8 June and 22 June, priced at 29.50 euros per person at Great Market. The hashtags place it as a halal Mediterranean brunch in Brussels. The fixed-date format means it runs as an event rather than a standing service.
items.author: little.brussels

items.title: The Wayne Café's menu, with a cautious halal and kosher note
items.synopsis: A halal-focused visit to The Wayne Café at Rue Van Eyck 30 in 1000 Brussels, covering a sweet menu of cakes, cookies and viennoiseries plus a savoury side of bagels, toasts and bowls. The creator had cake with a coffee and rated the combination highly. They report, explicitly flagged as second-hand information to treat with caution, that staff described the chicken as halal and the pastrami as kosher.
items.author: brusselshalalfood

items.title: Grande Piazza, the Italian of the moment
items.synopsis: A French review calling Grande Piazza the new Italian of the moment in Brussels, with a beautiful and well-conceived interior. The creator rates the whole run from starters to desserts a success, with music adding to the atmosphere. Prices are described as entirely reasonable, making it a girls-night or date venue.
items.author: odavintage

items.title: Bao Brussels on the Digue du Canal, halal
items.synopsis: A pin post for Bao Brussels at Digue du Canal 121 in 1070 Anderlecht, flagged halal. The caption contains the tag, address and food hashtags only. It is an address bookmark with no menu detail.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Zeyya's valet, rooftop and a now-closed competition
items.synopsis: A French post from an invited visit to Zeyya shortly after it opened, listing on-site parking, a valet service, a rooftop for warm days, very attentive staff and a striking room. The creator rates the food exquisite and the whole package built for a successful evening. The attached competition is marked finished.
items.author: unpeudelou

items.title: Old Boy reopens on rue de Tenbosch after renovation and a Bangkok trip
items.synopsis: Brussels Kitchen attends the reopening of Old Boy at 110 rue de Tenbosch in 1050 Brussels, a modern Thai restaurant that first opened in 2019 and had become one of the writer's favourites. It closed for several months for renovation, during which the team travelled to Bangkok. It has reopened with a larger space.
items.author: brusselskitchen

items.title: Manhattan Grill at Rogier, a halal steakhouse two weeks old
items.synopsis: A French visit to Manhattan Grill Brussels near Rogier, a halal steakhouse that had been open two weeks at the time of filming. It offers quality meats alongside halal versions of Belgian specialities. The meal opened with a parmesan fondue and the chef's scampi, which the creator calls generous.
items.author: labazeee

items.title: Uncaptioned reel from Zeyya
items.synopsis: A video posted by @zeyyarestaurant with no caption text. The account is the Brussels Greek-Lebanese-Turkish restaurant covered elsewhere in this folder. Nothing specific can be extracted from the post itself.
items.author: zeyyarestaurant

items.title: Rawa Bialyemen's 22-euro all-you-can-eat Yemeni buffet
items.synopsis: The transcript turns a bare booking pointer into the actual offer: an all-you-can-eat buffet at this Yemeni restaurant in Brussels for 22 euros. The spread covers a wide range of house-made dishes, including three kinds of slow-cooked meat, several varieties of rice and many wholly Yemeni starters. The creator stresses the offer runs only until the end of Ramadan and that booking is essential.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: A wood-fired pizzaiolo and 30-plus artisanal pizzas, maybe Brussels' best Italian
items.synopsis: A French review claiming the creator may have found the best Italian restaurant in Brussels, where a real pizzaiolo works a wood-fired oven. The meal opens with a Caesar salad, then spicy scampi diavola with house artisanal bread the creator scraped the plate clean of. More than thirty artisanal pizzas are made on site; the caption does not name the restaurant.
items.author: foodctrl.bx

items.title: An all-you-can-eat Sunday brunch buffet with drinks included
items.synopsis: A Sunday brunch running every week from 11:30 to 14:30, built as an all-you-can-eat buffet of freshly made hot and cold dishes, sweet and savoury, with cheese, bread, pastries, fruit and desserts. Tea, coffee and several juices are included in the formula. Children are welcome, which the creator flags as making it a family option; the caption does not name the venue.
items.author: downtown_colors

items.title: Ital Mercato in Sint-Pieters-Leeuw
items.synopsis: A minimal pin post for Ital Mercato at Burgemeesterstraat 7 in 1600 Sint-Pieters-Leeuw, just outside Brussels. The only descriptor is an Italian-food hashtag. It is an address-level bookmark.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Six Brussels rooftops already open, with hours and booking rules
items.synopsis: A rooftop roundup noting that not all Brussels terraces have opened yet, then listing six that are already running. Rooftop Perché at Chaussée de Charleroi 132 in 1060 Saint-Gilles is newly renovated, open daily 5pm to 1am with bookings on its own site; Secret Rooftop by Warwick at Rue Duquesnoy 5 runs daily 5pm to 11:30pm with last entry at 10:30 and takes no bookings; The8 Rooftop on Rue du Midi follows. The hours-and-bookings detail is what makes it usable.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Vertigo's Sunday boozy brunch with 90 minutes of free pour
items.synopsis: A disclosed invitation covering the Boozy Brunch at Vertigo, Rue de Rollebeek 7 in 1000 Brussels, every Sunday from 12:00 to 14:30. The drinks formula runs ninety minutes and is tiered: 15 euros for mimosa or soft drinks, 20 for prosecco or mocktails and 60 for Laurent Perrier champagne. The food is sharing plates, revisited brunch classics and desserts.
items.author: zooestories

items.title: Maison des Gaufres on Rue du Marché aux Herbes
items.synopsis: A pin post for Maison des Gaufres at Rue du Marché aux Herbes 109 in 1000 Brussels. The caption carries the tag, the address and food hashtags only. It is a waffle-stop bookmark in the tourist centre.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Basil's on Rue du Congrès, Neapolitan pizza and a closed 100-euro giveaway
items.synopsis: A post for Basil's Bruxelles at Rue du Congrès 31 in 1000 Brussels, which the creator rates among the best authentic Neapolitan pizzas in the city. The room is described as cosy and freshly decorated in Italian style. The attached giveaway for a 100-euro meal for two is marked closed.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Peach Pit in Schaarbeek, halal American food with a cheese-injected black burger
items.synopsis: A halal American diner at Peach Pit, Vleugelsstraat 40 in 1030 Schaarbeek, covering burgers and hotdogs. Prices run from 2.50 to 5 euros for starters, 8.90 to 18.90 for burger menus and 8.90 to 13.99 for hotdog menus. The signature oddity is a black burger you can inject with cheese yourself.
items.author: mangohagareats

items.title: Vitium's 28-euro lunch set menu, plus a meal-for-two giveaway
items.synopsis: A giveaway post for Vitium at Rue Edith Cavell 151 in 1180 Uccle, a modern Italian where the creator rates everything from starters to desserts. The practical detail is a new lunch set menu at 28 euros, available Tuesday to Saturday, covering starter, pasta or pizza and dessert, and changing regularly. Full pricing is on the restaurant's own site.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Zeyya, shared Greek, Lebanese and Turkish plates in a polished room
items.synopsis: A French review of Zeyya, a new Brussels restaurant serving sharing plates drawn from Greek, Lebanese and Turkish cooking. The standouts named are the mezze, a house tarama and sea bream in a salt crust. The creator gives a special mention to the atmosphere and the service.
items.author: _lanaomi

items.title: So Soir on Gyojasang, Korean street food with karaoke in central Brussels
items.synopsis: A magazine feature on Gyojasang, a new Korean restaurant in the heart of Brussels, framed as a dive into Korean street-food culture. Between the immersive decor, the food and the karaoke, the writers say it feels close to Seoul. The hashtags point to makgeolli, galbi, gimbap and bibimbap on the menu.
items.author: sosoirmagazine

items.title: The Wayne Café, coffee and art space on Rue Van Eyck
items.synopsis: A spot feature on The Wayne Café at Rue Van Eyck 30 in 1000 Brussels, positioned where coffee, art and culture meet. The framing is a feel-good venue doubling as an art space. It is pitched as a coffee-date and date-idea destination.
items.author: leatomic.be

items.title: Brussels world-cuisine reel carried by a Turkish song
items.synopsis: Transcription does not rescue this card: the audio is a Turkish song lyric and nothing else, so no venue, dish or neighbourhood is ever spoken. The caption only asks which countries to cover next in the Brussels world-cuisine series. The subject remains visual-only and unidentifiable from text.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Café Modelé, a new ceramic-painting café in the Marolles
items.synopsis: Part twenty of a favourite-places series, covering Café Modelé, a newly opened ceramic café in the heart of the Marolles. The format is painting your own ceramics over a cosy afternoon. The creator reports a very good session and is pleased with their own pieces.
items.author: unpeudelou

items.title: A giveaway for a Levantine meal for two at Restaurant Gabriel
items.synopsis: A competition post offering one reader a full meal for two at Restaurant Gabriel, serving Levantine cuisine in Brussels, on a date of their choosing. Entry requires following both accounts, liking the post and tagging a guest. The winner is to be drawn at random and announced in stories.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Rawa Bialyemen, Yemeni food in Brussels with a 20 percent discount
items.synopsis: A French recommendation for Rawa Bialyemen, described as a typical Yemeni restaurant in Brussels. The creator offers a twenty percent discount to anyone showing the video. The caption gives the offer and cuisine but no street address.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: Smoked-salmon waffles in a Belgian comics café
items.synopsis: A venue post for Muski Comics Café at Rue Froissart 13 in 1040 Etterbeek, whose hook is waffles topped with smoked salmon in a fully Belgian comic-book setting. It opens weekdays 8:00 to 18:00 and weekends 9:00 to 18:00. The concept pairs a savoury-waffle menu with comics decor.
items.author: muski.comics.cafe

items.title: Unlimited tiramisu at L'Annexe, Tour & Taxis
items.synopsis: A short post from L'Annexe at Tour & Taxis advertising unlimited tiramisu, with the creator urging viewers to hurry. The caption notes the offer is for adults only. It is a single-offer hook rather than a full venue review.
items.author: lannexetourettaxis

items.title: Six Brussels cafés with addresses, each dog-friendly
items.synopsis: A six-venue café list with full addresses: Le Café Leona at Av. Georges Henri 386 in Woluwe-Saint-Lambert, ZouZou at Rue des Colonies 18, Arsouille Café at Rue d'Alost 7, Koul Brussels at Quai du Hainaut 7 in Molenbeek, Flash Capsules at Rue des Chartreux 23, and Crema and More. Each entry is marked with a paw, indicating dogs are welcome. The caption asks which readers have already visited.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Les Fondus de la Raclette, cheese at the table
items.synopsis: An invited visit to Les Fondus de la Raclette in Brussels, where the creator jokes about the heat coming off the table-top raclette grills. The format is cheese-centred fondue and raclette service. It is a seasonal comfort-food venue bookmark.
items.author: _lanaomi

items.title: Wow Crab's seafood boils, priced by group size
items.synopsis: A venue post for Wow Crab at Rue du Fossé aux Loups 28B in 1000 Brussels, built around shared seafood boils. The tiers run 62 and 89.80 euros for one to two people, 105 and 128 for two to three, and 258 for four. Full menu and booking are on their website.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: La Laiterie in Parc Josaphat
items.synopsis: A short French post pinning La Laiterie, the café in Parc Josaphat in Brussels. The caption is the name, the park and café hashtags. It is a park-café bookmark with no menu detail.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: Scène, a hidden speakeasy for cocktails in central Brussels
items.synopsis: Part eighteen of a favourite-places series, featuring Scène, a concealed speakeasy in the centre of Brussels where the creator says elegance meets the craft of the cocktail. The atmosphere is hushed and the drinks are described as exquisite creations. It is pitched as a new date or night-out venue.
items.author: unpeudelou

items.title: Sunny Bao in Ixelles, halal chicken bao
items.synopsis: A French recommendation for Sunny Bao BXL at Chaussée de Vleurgat 157 box 16 in 1050 Ixelles. It opens Monday to Saturday from 11:00 to 19:00 and the chicken is halal. The hashtags place it as a Japanese-leaning spot in Brussels.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: Volaillerie Beldi's one-metre sandwich for four euros
items.synopsis: The transcript identifies the uncaptioned reel as a visit to Volaillerie Beldi in Brussels, which builds sandwiches a literal metre long. On the day of filming the remaining filling was minced beef mixed with chicken breast. The sandwich costs four euros, up from 2.50 before the cost-of-living squeeze, which the creator still calls reasonable, and the bulk of the clip is incredulous riffing on its size.
items.author: vidalalexe

items.title: Icosium, halal Algerian food on Rue des Hirondelles
items.synopsis: A pin post for Icosium Restaurant at Rue des Hirondelles 9 in 1000 Brussels, flagged halal with Algerian-cuisine hashtags. The caption carries the address and nothing else. It is a cuisine-and-address bookmark.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Gyoja Sang, Korean food plus karaoke rooms on rue Sainte-Catherine
items.synopsis: A venue post for Gyoja Sang at Rue Sainte-Catherine 8 in 1000 Brussels, open seven days a week from noon. Beyond the Korean menu it runs a photobooth at 6 euros for three photos and karaoke rooms with tiered minimum charges from 60 euros for up to four people to 12.50 per person for groups of eleven to sixteen. Vegetarian, vegan and halal options are available.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Hadj Said Berrada in Brussels
items.synopsis: A still image announcing an appearance by Hadj Said Berrada in Brussels, posted by an events account. The caption is a single line with no date, venue or ticketing detail. As an image post there is no audio track to recover further context from.
items.author: events.ma.officiel

items.title: Era, a Brussels date-night restaurant with a long order list
items.synopsis: A detailed order-by-order review of Era in Brussels, covering leek croquettes, chopped rump steak, sourdough breads, baby gem lettuce, charred hamachi sashimi, langoustine carpaccio, a flank steak and sweetbread skewer and dry-aged sirloin. The creator rates the leek croquettes incredibly creamy and the chopped rump steak an outright standout. They recommend adding it to a date-night list.
items.author: she.dreamsaboutfood

items.title: A comedy monologue roasting Toulouse, Antoine Dupont and Airbus
items.synopsis: The transcript shows this is a stand-up-style comedy reel about Toulouse, not a Brussels venue post. It runs through the Basilica of Saint-Sernin, the place du Capitole and Antoine Dupont as a monument you can visit free with the culture pass, then jokes that rugby is fifteen against fifteen except in Toulouse, where it is fifteen against Dupont. It closes on the city's Airbus dependency, with the line that one person in two works there and everyone else works for a subcontractor.
items.author: tombaldetti

items.title: Kings, a fully halal Korean barbecue where you run the grill
items.synopsis: A French feature on Kings, a one-hundred-percent halal Korean barbecue in Brussels where diners cook at the table. The marinated meats include beef bulgogi, soy beef and chicken marinated in mango and honey. The creator pitches it as an immersive outing for family or friends.
items.author: foodctrl.bx

items.title: Where to eat the world's third-best sandwich in central Brussels
items.synopsis: A shawarma post anchored on TasteAtlas rankings, which placed the sandwich third best in the world in 2024 and its toum sauce first in 2023. The creator declares for chicken shawarma with extra toum, the Lebanese garlic emulsion. The clip answers where to eat it in central Brussels.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Resto Lezee on Rue Wayez, Anderlecht
items.synopsis: A minimal pin post for Resto Lezee at Rue Wayez 19 in 1070 Anderlecht. The caption is the tag, the address and food hashtags only. It is an address-level bookmark with no menu detail.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Correspondance at Gare Maritime, by two-starred chef San Degeimbre
items.synopsis: A disclosed invitation covering Correspondance at Rue Picard 9, Pavillon 12 in Brussels' Gare Maritime, from double-Michelin-starred Belgian chef San Degeimbre. The cooking is described as simple with a touch of world-inspired creativity, in a setting built for relaxed eating. A lunch formula of starter and main is priced at 37 euros.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Matto, Mario Olimpio's flea-market-furnished Brussels restaurant
items.synopsis: A French visit to Matto, the latest venue from Mario Olimpio after the pasta at Primo and the painzas at Ciccio. The decor is assembled from flea-market and family finds, pulling diners into the owner's own world from the entrance. The creator frames the slightly mad atmosphere as entirely the point.
items.author: zooestories

items.title: Five Brussels dessert counters with prices, all with seating
items.synopsis: A five-venue dessert roundup with per-item prices: Virginia at 7.50 euros, Mains BXL at 5 per piece, Ginkgo Patisserie at 6.90, Bargello glacier at 7.50 and Swookies at 5. The creator stresses that all five offer dine-in rather than takeaway only. It is a directly comparable sweet-tooth shortlist.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Akai opens on the 30th floor of the Cardo with a panoramic view
items.synopsis: The opening of Akai Brussels, a rooftop restaurant, lounge bar and club on the thirtieth floor of the Cardo Brussels hotel at Av. du Boulevard 14 in 1210. The kitchen is Asian-Mediterranean fusion and the view is panoramic, including from the toilets. It opens Tuesday to Saturday for dinner only, with a DJ on Thursday, Friday and Saturday nights.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: La Mi Roger in Uccle, unlimited fondue with the prices listed
items.synopsis: A fondue night at La Mi Roger, Chaussée de Waterloo 798 in 1180 Uccle, with unlimited refills on both formulas. Fondue bourguignonne with beef, chimichurri chicken, salad, fries and four house sauces runs 29 euros per person; fondue savoyarde with charcuterie and baby potatoes is 32. Children pay 13 euros and house red wine is 6 euros a glass.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Testing the best pastries in Brussels, starting with Kaki Cake Bar
items.synopsis: A comparative pastry test across Brussels venues, opening with Kaki Cake Bar. The verdict favours their fluffy cheesecakes, with the sesame version singled out as light and delicate, and their Ka Baos rated excellent but a step below. The format is a ranked tasting rather than a single endorsement.
items.author: thesanta_house

items.title: Tonton Garby on Rue Duquesnoy, halal
items.synopsis: A minimal pin post for Tonton Garby at Rue Duquesnoy 6 in 1000 Brussels, flagged as halal. No dishes or prices appear in the caption. It is a bare address bookmark from a halal-focused account.
items.author: bonnes.adresses.bruxelles

items.title: Halal street food on rue de Flandre, with the full price list
items.synopsis: A French street-food recommendation at Rue de Flandre 17 in Brussels, halal with some vegetarian options. Prices are itemised: fried chicken from 9.50 euros with the popcorn version preferred, homemade lemonade at 5.50 with a yuzu the creator calls incredible, sides at 3.20 and wontons or gyoza at 10. It is pitched at visitors passing through.
items.author: mariustory

items.title: BAM Burger's UFO format, by an ex-Top Chef candidate
items.synopsis: A look at BAM Burger at Av. de la Couronne 459 in 1050 Ixelles and its so-called UFO burger packaging, which keeps the burger warm and juicy while letting you eat it without losing the filling. Ingredients are locally sourced and the combinations are described as original. They were devised by a former Top Chef candidate who also runs his own operation.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Belga Queen, dining inside an 18th-century bank with its vaults intact
items.synopsis: A venue feature on Belga Queen Brussels at Rue du Fossé aux Loups 32, housed in a former eighteenth-century bank. The original safes are still in place, which the creator says lets you experience the setting fully. It is filed as an architecture-led dining destination.
items.author: urban.maro

items.title: Esmero Alfajores, Argentine alfajores in Belgian chocolate
items.synopsis: A takeaway-only find at Esmero Alfajores, Av. Georges Henri 307 in 1200 Woluwe-Saint-Lambert, where Argentine alfajores meet Belgian chocolate. Prices are listed: a regular alfajor at 4.25 euros, a box of four at 17, five mini alfajores or five conitos at 15, and a 130g Frambú at 15. Orders are takeaway or online only.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Big Mamma lands in Brussels at Flagey
items.synopsis: A disclosed invitation post reacting to the arrival of the Big Mamma group in Brussels, in the Flagey area. The creator's framing is pure anticipation for the Italian chain's opening. It is a notable chain arrival rather than a dish review.
items.author: suchagirl

items.title: Carlo de Pascale on Vitium: all good, but the lighting is too bright
items.synopsis: A candid French review of Vitium that opens by stating plainly that everything is good. The critic praises three very Italian owners as kind, welcoming and passionate, and notes burrata appears throughout the menu. His one reservation is the decor's lighting, which overshoots the trendy-Italian look it aims for.
items.author: carlo_de_pascale

items.title: Vitium in Uccle, by two twenty-year veterans and an ex-CiPiAce chef
items.synopsis: A disclosed paid collaboration covering Vitium at Rue Edith Cavell 151 in 1180 Uccle, which blends Italian tradition with a modern creative streak. The team is Vito, Stefano and Gio, with Vito and Gio bringing more than twenty years in the trade and Stefano Rella arriving from a chef role elsewhere. The creator states the address was validated before any commitment.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Chinese hotpot at Quai au Bois à Brûler
items.synopsis: A French reel introducing hotpot to viewers who may not know the format, located at Quai au Bois à Brûler 55 in 1000 Brussels. The caption gives the pin and the cuisine and nothing more. It is a cuisine-discovery post with an address.
items.author: empereur_zi

items.title: Nami, handrolls passed hand to hand at the top of avenue Louise
items.synopsis: Food critic Carlo de Pascale reviews Nami, a concept that opened for the summer at the start of avenue Louise on the corner of rue Jourdan, an area he describes as crowded with restaurants of uneven interest. The makis are long-format with very crisp nori and good fillings. The handrolls are handed straight to the diner the moment the roll is finished, relay-style.
items.author: carlo_de_pascale

items.title: Koul Halal's first Brussels video visits Caffe Batavia
items.synopsis: The halal-food account's debut Brussels episode, visiting Caffe Batavia after heavy audience recommendation. The caption is a short intro with no menu detail. It corroborates Caffe Batavia as a widely recommended halal spot.
items.author: koul_halal

items.title: Torréfaction Van Dael, a coffee roaster in Laeken
items.synopsis: A spot feature on Torréfaction Van Dael at Rue Marie-Christine 134 in 1020 Brussels, in the Laeken district. The post is framed as a did-you-know-this-place discovery. It is a specialty coffee roastery rather than a café.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: L'Ultime Atome revives its all-you-can-eat buffet brunch in Saint-Boniface
items.synopsis: A French-language brunch report from L'Ultime Atome in the Saint-Boniface quarter, whose buffet formula had been discontinued and has now returned. An entire room is given over to the brunch, sweet and savoury, all made in house. The formula costs 35 euros per person for unlimited access to the buffet.
items.author: zooestories

items.title: Vitium, a brand-new Italian restaurant in Uccle
items.synopsis: A short French announcement of Vitium Bruxelles, a newly opened Italian restaurant in Uccle. The caption carries only the tag and the district. It is an early flag on an opening covered in more depth by other creators.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: The hidden Brussels restaurant whose chef turned down three Michelin stars
items.synopsis: The transcript explains the teaser caption: this is the story of a chef the video names as Sébastien Brasse, presented as the first to refuse the highest distinction in gastronomy, in order to take a layer of pressure off himself and his teams and concentrate on the cooking. The result is an intimate restaurant hidden at the top of a museum, serving exceptional food in a smart but very warm setting. Lunch is 50 euros, which the creator says is worth every euro.
items.author: leguideultime

items.title: Scopa Focacceria clears 200 focaccias in Brussels
items.synopsis: A thank-you post from Scopa Focacceria after a Brussels pop-up where all two hundred focaccias on offer were taken. The caption announces that the next event will mark their Leuven opening. It documents an expanding focaccia operation rather than a fixed Brussels address.
items.author: scopa_focacceria

items.title: Bros, a tiny Sicilian counter in Ixelles with posted prices
items.synopsis: A venue post for Bros at Av. de la Couronne 431 in 1050 Ixelles, described as a little Italian gem where everything is delizioso. It is a very small space working both takeaway and dine-in, open Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 21:00. Prices are itemised: pizza slice 6.50 euros, arancini 3.90, focaccia 6.90 and a pistaccino at 5.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Chez Sun in Etterbeek, Cantonese, Thai and Vietnamese under 18 euros
items.synopsis: A venue post for Chez Sun at Chaussée de Wavre 657 in 1040 Etterbeek, serving simple Cantonese, Thai and Vietnamese dishes. All mains fall between ten and eighteen euros, with starters at four to six euros and four chicken nems for five. It opens daily from noon to 11pm for dine-in or takeaway.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Rosita's Cantina, homemade Mexican in Brussels
items.synopsis: A French-language review of Rosita's Cantina, framed through the creator's Coco-inspired obsession with Mexican food. The traditional dishes are made in-house, generous and well executed. The creator jokes it would have wrecked their budget had they known it sooner.
items.author: paupo__

items.title: Lalla Shama, traditional Moroccan breakfast in Uccle
items.synopsis: A venue post for Restaurant Lalla Shama at Av. De Fré 205 in 1180 Uccle, serving a traditional Moroccan breakfast and brunch. It opens Tuesday to Sunday from 9am to 2pm with six set formulas priced at 7, 9, 15.50 and 19 euros, plus extras from 2.50 to 7 euros. The pricing detail makes it directly plannable.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: The Guide Brussels' September events agenda
items.synopsis: A monthly carousel listing things to do in Brussels during September, from the account's recurring agenda format. Readers are pointed to weekly Thursday updates in the story highlights for additions. It is a time-bound events digest rather than evergreen content.
items.author: theguide_brussels

items.title: Nénu in Saint-Gilles, chef Robin's twisted Vietnamese plates
items.synopsis: Brussels Kitchen names Nénu at 21 rue Dejoncker in 1060 Saint-Gilles as a personal top-of-the-shortlist restaurant. Chef Robin cooks Vietnamese dishes with a restrained twist, with lamb and smoked-eel wontons called out as the signature. Banh cuon are also described as permanent menu fixtures.
items.author: brusselskitchen

items.title: A Brussels brunch on rue de Rolbeek with veggie options and no queue
items.synopsis: A French-language brunch review of a venue at rue de Rolbeek 30 in Brussels, with plenty of vegetarian and vegan choices and mains between nine and eighteen euros. The creator's picks are the red-berries pancakes and the burrata toast. They note it opens daily and they faced no queue.
items.author: mariustory

items.title: ZouZou in Ixelles, all-day brunch and burgers with no reservations
items.synopsis: A venue post for ZouZou at Rue Bouré 10 in 1050 Ixelles, serving all-day brunch and burgers. Opening hours run Tuesday to Saturday 10:00 to 21:00 and Sunday 10:00 to 18:00. The caption states clearly that no reservations are taken.
items.author: zouzoubrussels

items.title: Akai Brussels teases a sushi opening
items.synopsis: A pre-opening teaser from Akai Brussels promising sushi artistry and sophisticated interiors, billed as the city's new icon. No address or opening date is given. It is an opening to watch rather than a visitable venue.
items.author: akai_brussels

items.title: Urban Karaoke comes to Jardin Ayana
items.synopsis: A carousel announcing an Urban Karaoke night hosted at Jardin Ayana in Brussels on the coming Sunday, staged outdoors under the stars. The invitation is explicitly open to both singers and spectators. It pairs an event series with a garden venue.
items.author: jardinayana

items.title: Urban Karaoke returns on 6 September
items.synopsis: An event announcement for the return of Urban Karaoke in Brussels on 6 September. The pitch is showing off your talent and sharing a musical evening with friends and family. It is a dated nightlife event rather than a venue review.
items.author: urbankaraoke.bxl

items.title: Brunch Corner in Grand-Bigard, just outside Brussels
items.synopsis: An invited tasting at the newly opened Brunch Corner in Grand-Bigard, a short way outside Brussels. The visuals centre on pancakes, berries and shakes. It is a brunch option for anyone willing to leave the city centre.
items.author: laureendlb

items.title: Uncaptioned reel from Serenitea Room Brussels
items.synopsis: A video posted by @serenitearoombrussels with no caption text at all. The account points to a tea room in Brussels. Nothing more can be determined without the video content.
items.author: serenitearoombrussels

items.title: L'Express tested as the best shoarma in Belgium
items.synopsis: A Dutch-language verdict putting L'Express in Brussels 1000 to the test as the best shoarma in Belgium. The caption is a single line with the location pin. The reasoning is in the video rather than the text.
items.author: gafourakrz

items.title: Halal Korean K-TOAST at Caffe Batavia near De Brouckère
items.synopsis: A French-language review of the new K-TOAST at Caffe Batavia in Brussels, available in Korean chicken, beef bulgogi, tempura prawn and vegan versions. The creator chose the Korean chicken with kimchi, yuzu sauce and house mayo and recommends it unreservedly. The meeting point given is De Brouckère.
items.author: brusselshalalfood

items.title: Sekaï Corndogs, customisable halal corndogs and melon pan
items.synopsis: A new-opening post for Sekaï Corndogs, offering halal corndogs you configure yourself plus Japanese desserts such as melon pan. Two Brussels addresses are given: Rue de Malines 50 and Rue de l'Enseignement 72, both near Rue Neuve and City 2. It is a halal-friendly Japanese street-food find.
items.author: foodctrl.bx

items.title: BadBun near Flagey, billed as the capital's best chicken burger
items.synopsis: A French-language review naming BadBun, a few steps from place Flagey, as the reference point for chicken burgers in Brussels. Its distinguishing feature is breaded chicken thigh rather than the usual breast. The creator treats it as the category benchmark.
items.author: labazeee

items.title: One-euro brochettes at Stacked in Ixelles, Friday and Saturday late
items.synopsis: A French-language find at Stacked in Ixelles, where marinated turkey brochettes cost one euro on Friday and Saturday nights from 22:00. The euro buys the skewer plus bread, chimichurri and two house sauces. The creator also pushes their halal pastrami sandwiches.
items.author: labazeee

items.title: BS40 on Rue au Beurre, Japanese-leaning chocolate
items.synopsis: A short pin post for BS40 at Rue au Beurre 40 in central Brussels. The hashtags point to chocolate with a Japanese influence, and the visual is a dango-style sweet. The caption carries no further detail.
items.author: decouverte_de_sarah

items.title: Prince de Liège steakhouse in Anderlecht
items.synopsis: A promotional post for the Prince de Liège steakhouse at Chaussée de Ninove 664 in 1070 Anderlecht. The offer covers steak, burgers and grilled meat. It is a straightforward venue bookmark with an address.
items.author: princedeliege.brussels

items.title: Au Laboureur Steak House, aged Black Angus and Kobe in Saint-Gilles
items.synopsis: A venue post from Au Laboureur Steak House at Boulevard Jamar 1A in 1060 Saint-Gilles, built around meat ageing and maturation. The range runs from Black Angus to Kobe beef. Phone and email contact details are in the caption.
items.author: aulaboureur.brussels

items.title: Four tested breakfast spots in Brussels
items.synopsis: A French-language breakfast guide naming four Brussels venues the creator has personally tested, each chosen for a specific reason. The first is Café Le Refuge on place Saint-Job in Uccle. The format addresses how hard it is to pick from the city's crowded breakfast offer.
items.author: bruxellesatable

items.title: Connecting Vinted to Chinese suppliers with zero stock
items.synopsis: A French post teaching step-by-step sourcing direct from China to sell on French marketplaces. The specific hook, gated behind commenting ECOM, is connecting Vinted to Chinese suppliers. The model is pitched as requiring zero stock and zero advertising spend.
items.author: sunecomm

items.title: Five free repos that turn Claude into a designer
items.synopsis: A post crediting @nateherkai for publishing five free repositories that give Claude design capability, with the creator's own workflow sent to anyone commenting DESIGN. The creator says they tested all five on a shop that had a 4.9-star rating but no website, and calls the result surreal. The claim is a design pipeline assembled entirely from free components.
items.author: henrychua

items.title: Sourcing super-clone watches in Guangzhou
items.synopsis: A digital-nomad field report on sourcing super-clone watches in Guangzhou, China. The hashtags reference Rolex, Audemars Piguet and Patek as the models being replicated. The caption states the activity without detailing vendors or prices.
items.author: digitalnomadpov

items.title: Anthropic's Model Hardware Standard lets agents drive any machine
items.synopsis: A post on Anthropic's release of the Model Hardware Standard, which lets any AI agent discover and operate any machine without someone writing custom code for every device. The creator lists launch partners including Genentech, Carnegie Mellon, HHMI Janelia, QuEra, Universal Robots, Danaher, AWS, Raspberry Pi and Hugging Face. The argued significance is that software was the easy part, while every lab instrument and factory machine speaks its own language.
items.author: atlasberry008

items.title: Google Pomelli builds brand campaigns from your site URL
items.synopsis: The creator presents Pomelli, a free Google Labs marketing tool he says can replace a design team. You paste your website URL and the AI analyses your visual identity, covering style, colours and fonts, then automatically generates campaign ideas and visuals consistent with that brand. Everything remains customisable including images, text and colours, with the link gated behind commenting google.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: Made-to-measure sewing patterns generated from your own measurements
items.synopsis: Part 113 of the creator's "sites to kill boredom" series walks through the whole flow: pick a garment model, enter your own measurements, and the site drafts a bespoke sewing pattern you can then adjust to taste before exporting it in the file format of your choice. The appeal is skipping standard sizing entirely for home sewing. The site itself is only shown on screen and never named aloud or in the caption, so the URL has to be read off the video.
items.author: planeteia

items.title: Outfit swapping plus talking-video generation from one photo
items.synopsis: The creator describes changing outfits on any model with AI and producing ultra-realistic talking videos from the result. The stated flow is to upload a photo, add clothing, generate variations and then make the subject speak, all within minutes. A full prompt sheet and the link are gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: JS Box Manufacturer's magnetic flat-folding gift boxes
items.synopsis: A B2B packaging post from JS Box Manufacturer showcasing bespoke magnetic folding gift boxes that ship flat as one piece. The range includes a triangular magnetic folding box described as portable and elegant for high-end brand packaging, plus a rectangular magnetic version. Target categories named are perfume, jewellery, skincare and cosmetics.
items.author: jsboxmanufacturer1

items.title: A YouTube automation channel run by Claude Desktop and n8n MCP
items.synopsis: The creator argues you no longer need writers, editors, voiceover artists and thumbnail designers to run a YouTube channel, because Claude plus n8n can automate the system from your desktop. The specific architecture he names is installing Claude Desktop locally and connecting it to the n8n MCP server, at which point the whole content pipeline becomes AI-driven. The step-by-step breakdown is gated behind following and commenting GUIDE.
items.author: kayvon.ai

items.title: Google Cloud compendium of 601 real-world gen-AI use cases
items.synopsis: The post points to a free Google Cloud resource collecting more than six hundred concrete generative-AI deployments across industries, from product to operations to marketing. The creator frames it as an organised field manual rather than another scattered ideas list, with real deployments and outcomes instead of speculation. Access is gated behind commenting the word AI.
items.author: kyleherbel

items.title: Caligula Vintage sells tracksuits online, open seven days
items.synopsis: A French post from Caligula Vintage in Brussels pitching tracksuits, with the shop link in the account bio. The store is described as open seven days a week. The hashtags mark it as a humorous point-of-view format.
items.author: caligulavintage

items.title: A Chinese body-kit factory that ages a 2007 X5 into a 2024
items.synopsis: The transcript is about car facelift kits rather than the clothing sourcing the hashtags suggest, and it names the factory. The car shown is a 2007 X5 converted with a full kit, and the creator recommends a Chinese plant he pronounces as Shenzhou Fueto Molded Plastics, specialising in facelifts and complete body kits for German SUVs and saloons, reachable directly on Alibaba. His market explanation is that the Maghreb and Middle East tax new cars so heavily that converting an old model beats paying some 30,000 euros more for a new one, and he rates the parts and interior finish as manufacturer quality.
items.author: verso_supply

items.title: Aircela's fridge-sized machine that makes fuel from air
items.synopsis: A French explainer on Aircela, a startup that has unveiled a refrigerator-sized machine shown producing fuel using only ambient air. The pitch is no petroleum, no drilling and no pollution, yielding a fuel usable in any combustion-engine car. The video sets out how the process works.
items.author: bloom_media.fr

items.title: CreaShort connects an AI agent to your social accounts end to end
items.synopsis: A French post on CreaShort, which the creator says lets you fully automate videos for TikTok, Instagram and YouTube by connecting a single agent. That agent handles the script, the images, the voiceover, the edit and even publishes the video directly. The creator also frames it as connecting ChatGPT to an Instagram account, with the link sent on request.
items.author: leoodeep

items.title: Building an online business with Emergent, part nine
items.synopsis: The ninth instalment of a French series on little-known websites, claiming that creating an online business has never been easier than with this one. The caption body does not name it, but the hashtags identify Emergent AI. It is positioned as an app-building shortcut for founders.
items.author: planeteia

items.title: A four-step chain for consistent AI characters
items.synopsis: The creator gives his character-consistency pipeline step by step with every tool named. Step one is a free GPT fed basic details such as age, style and vibe, which writes the character prompt automatically; step two drops that prompt into Seedream 3.0, which he rates the best text-to-image model, yielding four character options. Step three takes the chosen image into Magnific AI to fix the plastic AI skin texture so the character reads as an actual person.
items.author: ashokreddyai

items.title: How DTF printing changed custom design production
items.synopsis: A French post on direct-to-film printing technology and how it has transformed the way businesses and individuals produce custom designs. The caption frames it as an invitation to learn more. It identifies the technology category rather than a specific vendor.
items.author: electronics_rounder

items.title: Building a complete fashion campaign in Flora Fauna AI
items.synopsis: A Portuguese-language tutorial on Flora Fauna AI, arguing that with the right prompts you can assemble a full visual narrative look by look and scene by scene inside the tool. The walkthrough builds a fashion sequence from scratch: one character, then another, then both together as though it were a campaign. It emphasises multimodal generation with advanced models and a finished look.
items.author: human___academy

items.title: Ordering from Taobao without a private agent, with shipping costs
items.synopsis: The transcript gives the actual tutorial: buying from Taobao through the AllChinaBuy platform rather than paying a private agent. You register with an email and password, pick your product and check the quality yourself, set delivery to France and tick the photo-inspection option before paying and choosing a shipping line. The creator recommends the two-week line at roughly ten to twelve euros per kilo.
items.author: sk_resellfr

items.title: One-click AI video cloning to replace a 800-dollar-a-year tool stack
items.synopsis: The transcript sets out the workflow behind the income claim. You copy the link of a high-performing faceless video, paste it in and click Generate Script, then pick an image style, a voiceover and music and click Generate Video, producing a finished clip in seconds ready to download and post. The creator's pitch is that this replaces separate Midjourney, ChatGPT, ElevenLabs and CapCut subscriptions costing around eight hundred dollars a year; the tool itself is still only named behind the comment gate.
items.author: mattuncut

items.title: Caps at 50 cents a piece on a 10,000-unit closeout
items.synopsis: The transcript reveals a supplier pitch rather than a sourcing lesson. The seller, who says they are a current supplier in China, is clearing caps in many styles at fifty cents each on a final run of ten thousand pieces. They point to the fabric and detailing as evidence of quality and suggest a resale price of five to ten dollars in the buyer's own market.
items.author: achourisourcing

items.title: Riona, a free open-source AI agent that runs your social accounts
