items.synopsis: The post presents Clever AI Humanizer as a tool that rewrites AI-generated text in seconds, with the explicit purpose of tricking AI detectors. The creator frames it as essential for ChatGPT users. The tool is named directly in the caption, with no usage detail beyond the claim.
items.author: codewithharshad

items.title: Ranking automations by ROI instead of building on vibes
items.synopsis: The creator names three reasons AI automations fail: automating tasks that take ten minutes, not knowing the actual ROI, and building on vibes rather than data. His prescribed method is to map every business process in Notion, rank them by ROI with a specific Claude prompt, then visualise the result as a diagram with a second prompt. He reports what this surfaces in practice: monthly reporting costing 97,000 dollars a year, client onboarding 41,000 and support tickets 27,000.
items.author: alassafi.ai

items.title: Replacing background, lighting and clothing in video with Runway Aleph
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates swapping the background, lighting and clothing inside existing video footage using AI. The hashtags identify Runway Aleph as the model, along with its in-context add, remove and transform operations, camera-angle changes and scene relighting. The links are gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: rourke

items.title: A hundred AI agents built in a single day
items.synopsis: A one-line claim of building one hundred AI agents in a day, tagged for n8n and automation. No agent type, method or outcome is described. The substance is in the video.
items.author: liambuilds.ai

items.title: Context engineering has displaced prompt engineering
items.synopsis: The creator argues that despite the continued talk about prompt engineering, that is no longer where the leverage lies; the differentiating skill is context engineering. What matters is not how you write the prompt but the information environment you build around the model: the order of data, the structure, the memory and how you guide its reasoning. He cites Anthropic, LangChain and Manus as having shown in their published work that mastering context produces more reliable, autonomous and coherent agents.
items.author: robinbride.ia

items.title: Lupa upscaler promising real skin texture at 6K
items.synopsis: The tool account promotes its own upscaler on three claims: real skin texture, perfect lighting and 6K definition. The product is identifiable from the account and the gate word, Lupa. No comparison or sample workflow is given beyond the claims.
items.author: lupaupscaler

items.title: Google Pomelli builds brand campaigns from your site URL
items.synopsis: The creator presents Pomelli, a free Google Labs marketing tool he says can replace a design team. You paste your website URL and the AI analyses your visual identity, covering style, colours and fonts, then automatically generates campaign ideas and visuals consistent with that brand. Everything remains customisable including images, text and colours, with the link gated behind commenting google.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: Outfit swapping plus talking-video generation from one photo
items.synopsis: The creator describes changing outfits on any model with AI and producing ultra-realistic talking videos from the result. The stated flow is to upload a photo, add clothing, generate variations and then make the subject speak, all within minutes. A full prompt sheet and the link are gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Six steps to consistent AI anime with Nano Banana and Seedance
items.synopsis: The creator outlines building AI anime in six steps using Nano Banana together with Seedance for consistent characters and full animations. The method is to start from a source image then alternate between the two tools, Seedance handling multi-shot scenes and Nano Banana rendering detailed anime frames. Repeating that alternation is how the animation is extended, with the full guide gated behind commenting ANIME.
items.author: skaigenerated

items.title: An AI hedge-fund Telegram bot for portfolio management
items.synopsis: The post discusses version two of an AI-powered hedge fund Telegram bot that lets users manage an investment portfolio through chat commands. Its stated functions are analysing assets, providing investment advice and tracking performance, integrating several financial data sources. The hashtags place the build on n8n.
items.author: greymatter_ai

items.title: Claude Skills is the innovation behind the SKILLS gate
items.synopsis: The unnamed innovation turns out to be Claude Skills, which the creator frames as a toolbox Claude can reach into on its own and which he stresses is free. His examples: feed it five of your LinkedIn posts and it writes in your voice, feed it your company information and it answers customer questions, and it can produce Excel files, PowerPoint decks and code. He walks through creating a skill from his last ten LinkedIn posts and a second one carrying his brand for slide generation — Claude authors the skill itself, then picks it up automatically in later conversations.
items.author: slama.ai

items.title: A YouTube automation channel run by Claude Desktop and n8n MCP
items.synopsis: The creator argues you no longer need writers, editors, voiceover artists and thumbnail designers to run a YouTube channel, because Claude plus n8n can automate the system from your desktop. The specific architecture he names is installing Claude Desktop locally and connecting it to the n8n MCP server, at which point the whole content pipeline becomes AI-driven. The step-by-step breakdown is gated behind following and commenting GUIDE.
items.author: kayvon.ai

items.title: Diffussion auto-removes filler from clips in CapCut
items.synopsis: The creator presents Diffussion, a free tool that polishes clips using CapCut and vibe coding rather than manual editing. The workflow he describes is minimal: drop your clips in, hit Clean, and it automatically removes filler and optimises shots, then one click accepts the changes and you export. A setup guide is gated behind commenting WOW.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Smooth AI transitions built in LTX Studio
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates creating smooth transitions with AI and tags LTX Studio as the tool. The caption names the platform and the effect but describes no settings or prompts. The link is gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: rourke

items.title: Claude Desktop wired to the n8n API builds whole workflows from one prompt
items.synopsis: The transcript lays out the full setup the caption only gestured at: install Claude Desktop and Node.js, paste the supplied command into a terminal, then in Claude's Settings → Developer → Edit Config add the MCP server block and substitute your own n8n instance URL and a freshly created n8n API key. A project called "n8n Builder" is then given a long system prompt as its instructions. After restarting Claude, plain-text requests produce complete, ready-to-import n8n agents — the prompt itself stays behind a comment gate.
items.author: greymatter_ai

items.title: Timeline Prompting to fix weak Sora 2 output
items.synopsis: The creator argues one change fixes bad Sora 2 video, a technique he calls Timeline Prompting, and gives the structure outright. Step one splits the video by seconds like a director rather than dumping random prompts: 0-3s hook, 3-6s context, 6-9s peak, 9-12s CTA or resolution, which builds attention flow instead of chaos. Step two adds control tags per layer, with CAM for camera movement, VO for voice, MUSIC for sound design and EMOTION for tone.
items.author: tapewarp.ai

items.title: A 360-degree branded product promo pipeline ending in Kling
items.synopsis: The creator outlines turning product promos into polished brand visuals with AI across multiple angles. The steps named are generating a 360-degree view, creating branded items such as bags and caps that look professionally produced, then merging those visuals into a photo-exhibition presentation. Kling AI is used to bring the stills to life, with links gated behind commenting HUMAN.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: An all-in-one text, image and video tool with no subscription
items.synopsis: The creator promotes a single AI tool covering text, image and even video generation, claiming no subscription and no limits. The product is never named in the caption. The link is sent to anyone commenting IA.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Buy It in ChatGPT turns the assistant into a storefront
items.synopsis: The creator leads a news roundup with OpenAI launching Buy It in ChatGPT, powered by Stripe and a new Agentic Commerce Protocol. US users can purchase directly from Etsy sellers, with over a million Shopify merchants including Glossier, SKIMS and Spanx to follow, making ChatGPT a direct competitor to Amazon and Google. His actionable advice for sellers is to prepare structured product data and test integrations early, alongside headlines on Anthropic shipping a leading coding model and Lovable claiming its update killed software developers.
items.author: tenex_labs

items.title: Wan 2.2 Animate, open-source character-driven animation
items.synopsis: The post shows output from Wan 2.2 Animate, described as the first open-source model focused specifically on character-driven animation. Its two stated uses are animating any still image and swapping any character into an existing video. The caption identifies the model and its purpose without detailing the pipeline.
items.author: theaisavvy

items.title: Google Cloud compendium of 601 real-world gen-AI use cases
items.synopsis: The post points to a free Google Cloud resource collecting more than six hundred concrete generative-AI deployments across industries, from product to operations to marketing. The creator frames it as an organised field manual rather than another scattered ideas list, with real deployments and outcomes instead of speculation. Access is gated behind commenting the word AI.
items.author: kyleherbel

items.title: OpenAI ships a free prompt optimizer for GPT-5
items.synopsis: The creator recommends the official OpenAI prompt optimizer and pastes the direct platform URL in the caption rather than gating it. The link targets the GPT-5 model with optimisation enabled. He points to a longer YouTube video for the walkthrough.
items.author: paytonbilodeau

items.title: A nine-tool production chain for one short film
items.synopsis: The creator documents his full workflow for a single piece, numbering each stage. He planned the off-camera reveal and refined the idea with ChatGPT, generated characters in Seedream, changed poses in Nano Banana, upscaled with Topaz and animated in VEO3. Voices were fixed in ElevenLabs, editing done in CapCut with a transition frame from Kling, and finished with an Apple frame, music and colour grade, as day 345 of 365.
items.author: tumifnx

items.title: A copyable prompt for advanced JSON image profiles
items.synopsis: The creator publishes the full prompt in the caption rather than gating it, instructing the model to decode an image into code with savage precision. It demands maximum detail, defining everything possible including the vibe, mood and style, and asks the model to think like a professional photographer and colour-grading expert. The closing instruction is to take its time because the task is about detail, not speed.
items.author: growhouse.co

items.title: Plain-English video prompting on a V4.0 model, site unnamed
items.synopsis: The transcript explains the alternative to JSON prompting but never names the website, so the post stays unreproducible. You select a V4.0 model in the dashboard and write ordinary sentences instead of a prompt structure, his examples being a Coca-Cola bottle transforming into a diner, a Nutella jar exploding into a full breakfast and an IKEA box unfolding into furniture. Edits work the same way, with instructions such as adding a cheering sound effect or making the transformation faster.
items.author: harshhhgautam

items.title: A four-step chain for consistent AI characters
items.synopsis: The creator gives his character-consistency pipeline step by step with every tool named. Step one is a free GPT fed basic details such as age, style and vibe, which writes the character prompt automatically; step two drops that prompt into Seedream 3.0, which he rates the best text-to-image model, yielding four character options. Step three takes the chosen image into Magnific AI to fix the plastic AI skin texture so the character reads as an actual person.
items.author: ashokreddyai

items.title: ChatGPT writes the prompt, Claude writes the n8n workflow
items.synopsis: The transcript explains the two-model chain the caption only thanked Claude for. You first ask ChatGPT to write a very precise prompt aimed at Claude, requesting JSON for an n8n workflow, and state there what the workflow must do. You copy that generated prompt into Claude, which writes the whole workflow as JSON. Copying the JSON and pasting it onto a blank n8n canvas materialises the complete, ready-to-use workflow, which the creator stresses took only these two models.
items.author: mats.automation

items.title: Genspark called the most remarkable AI tool available
items.synopsis: The creator names Genspark as the most impressive AI tool he has used and says he is eager for future updates, predicting it will change work, school and business. The caption is enthusiasm plus the product name, with no feature breakdown. The demonstration is in the video.
items.author: imjonathanacuna

items.title: Website cloning, explainer animations and AI influencers, none named
items.synopsis: The transcript walks all three tools without naming any of them, so the AI comment gate is never opened. The first copies a site from its URL, demonstrated on nike.com and described as coding almost the whole thing into a customisable clone. The second turns a confusion such as linear equations into a narrated animation, explaining y equals mx plus b, the intercept and the slope as rise over run, and also accepts an uploaded PDF. The third builds an AI influencer from preferences and prompts, generates its content and chats with fans.
items.author: harshhhgautam

items.title: Building Lightroom presets from any film's colour palette
items.synopsis: The transcript delivers an editing method the caption never mentioned. Search online for a film's colour palette, Oppenheimer in his example, and save the resulting swatch image, then attach it to ChatGPT with a specific prompt: create a Lightroom preset from the attachment colours, output as an XMP file, editing hue, saturation and luminance to represent those colours and adjusting colour grade, white balance and a matching curve. ChatGPT returns the XMP, which imports straight into Lightroom, and he notes it works from any film, game or source whose palette you can find.
items.author: c.vladmanea

items.title: A free end-to-end website workflow ending in Webflow
items.synopsis: The creator shares a step-by-step AI workflow for building websites quickly and at no cost, starting with brainstorming ideas in ChatGPT and generating custom graphics with free AI tools. The bonus step is exporting the finished design into Webflow for development handoff. A separate list of his preferred tools is gated behind commenting AI tools.
items.author: filatov.design

items.title: Krea AI for real-time photo editing then video
items.synopsis: The creator names the tool outright in the caption, Krea AI, and describes editing photos in real time with AI before converting them into video. He credits another artist for the Porsche GT RS poster design used as the example. The link is additionally gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: rourke

items.title: Imagen 3 for the character, Viggle V3 for the motion
items.synopsis: The transcript fills in the whole two-tool pipeline. The character is made in Google Imagen 3, which he notes has just been updated, is completely free and is much improved, and he mentions Google also launched Whisk, which lets you prompt with images; for Imagen you type the prompt, often drafted with ChatGPT, and get four options. He then takes a video of himself to Viggle and its new V3 model, uploading the video and the image and clicking create, with roughly three free generations, 9.99 a month, and a creator programme offering free credits.
items.author: benkaluza

items.title: Krea AI for Reels visuals and animation
items.synopsis: The creator presents Krea AI as a way to produce eye-catching visuals and animations instantly for Instagram Reels. He positions it for creators wanting stronger storytelling and creative edits, and specifically mentions music videos as a fit. The link is gated behind commenting INSTANT.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Stress-testing Runway video-to-video on a Matrix fight scene
items.synopsis: The creator deliberately pushed Runway video-to-video using a live-action kung fu scene from The Matrix. His pipeline is explicit: he replaced his own face into the original scene using Face Fusion with face enhance for smoothing, then fed that into Runway and experimented. He chose the scene precisely because multiple characters, fast movement and changing angles should challenge the model, and reports being pleasantly surprised at how well it held up.
items.author: techguyver

items.title: nomorecopyright.com regenerates a lookalike of a paid image
items.synopsis: The transcript names the service as nomorecopyright.com and explains the mechanism the caption left vague: you drop in the original copyrighted image, choose a size and hit generate, and it returns a new AI image modelled on it that you download and use. The creator contrasts this with paying for the stock photo or risking a per-image fine. The claim that the output is legally clear is his alone and is not substantiated.
items.author: torro.io

items.title: Google Earth as a substitute for drone footage
items.synopsis: The creator argues you do not need a drone to get aerial shots, with Google Earth named in the hashtags as the substitute. The pitch is aimed at filmmakers and editors wanting sweeping establishing shots for free. The technique itself is demonstrated in the video.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: An unnamed site aggregating tools across every discipline
items.synopsis: The transcript describes the breadth without identifying the site. It claims to cover coding tools, website design on request, presentations, video editing and graphic design, essentially any task, with what the creator calls endless tools in one place. The link goes only to followers who comment tools.
items.author: harshhhgautam

items.title: The ACDQ formula for structuring any ChatGPT prompt
items.synopsis: The creator lays out a four-part prompting formula he calls ACDQ, spelling each letter out in the caption. A is for act, telling the AI to operate as a specialist; C is context, giving it as much background as possible; D is depth, asking it to think deeply for insightful responses. Q is questions, letting the AI draw the best insights out of you, which he frames as the route to genuine collaboration rather than one-shot requests.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Rollout builds a complete website from a spoken brief
items.synopsis: The transcript turns a three-word caption into a specific product: rollout.site. The creator frames it against the agency process, where you brief a designer, review concepts, iterate on colours, logo and pages, and wait three to four months for a decent site. Instead you write a few lines describing what you want, in his example an Amazon-style storefront selling given products in given colours, and two minutes later the whole site exists with photos, features and colours in place.
items.author: manikarthik

items.title: Part eighty-five of a websites series, featuring Vidu AI
items.synopsis: Entry eighty-five in a long-running series on powerful websites, this one about making videos effortlessly in a few clicks. The hashtags name viduai, identifying Vidu AI as the tool. No workflow detail appears in the caption.
items.author: beasttechx

items.title: Blingshot generates royalty-free logos with no email
items.synopsis: The transcript names the site the caption hid: blingshot.io, which generates royalty-free, usable images in seconds, free and without handing over an email address. The creator demonstrates prompting in French, asking for a therapist logo on a beige background as a genuine one-shot first attempt, and rates the result remarkable for the speed and price. A second test, a cat fishing in an igloo, renders in seconds and downloads with a single save.
items.author: becomethegirl

items.title: An unnamed multi-agent site that builds a project from one sentence
items.synopsis: The transcript shows what the tool does but withholds its name, so the post stays unverifiable. You type the task you want, his example being an alarm app that donates to charity each time you hit snooze, and the site spawns cooperating AI agents, delegating research to one bot and the front end to another while showing which subtasks are running, pending or done. A results tab then returns the details and ready-to-use code.
items.author: carlodigital_

items.title: The one thing AI will never do for you is think
items.synopsis: The creator grants that AI is remarkable but insists it will never do your thinking, and that this is the most neglected part. He admits building entire workflows where research, analysis and writing are all handled by AI without lifting a finger. His conclusion is that even a perfect workflow has one weak link, the human supervising it, which he illustrates with an AI-run blog whose ideas and content look sound.
items.author: aurel.ia.scheck

items.title: Pika named for try-on, 4K portraits and VFX
items.synopsis: The transcript identifies the website as Pika, which the caption kept behind an AI comment. The creator describes three uses: uploading a photo of yourself plus a background and a garment to try clothing on, generating 4K visuals of yourself from one photo and a text prompt, and producing Hollywood-level VFX shots that would be impossible to film, again from a photo and a prompt. He says it can be started for free.
items.author: rourke

items.title: How ManyChat turns comment bait into automated DMs
items.synopsis: The transcript explains the mechanic behind every comment-the-word post: when you comment the trigger word you receive an automatic DM within seconds, and the tool doing it is ManyChat. The creator is explicit about why creators use it beyond delivery, namely that it manufactures comment volume, which pushes Instagram to distribute the video further, so it both lifts views and sells around the clock. He then walks the setup: link your Instagram, go to Automations, click New Automation, select the trigger user comments on your post or reel, pick the post, set the keyword and write the message to send.
items.author: joshbutcheronline

items.title: Maneken turns a flat design into product mockups by drag and drop
items.synopsis: The transcript identifies the hidden-websites list first entry as maneken.app and shows what it does. You drag your image onto a product to create the mockup, and can repeat it across different designs and products. The demonstration drops a design onto a billboard, which renders immediately and stays easy to edit afterwards.
items.author: onlinemarket2522

items.title: Gemini via Google AI Studio with a two-million-token window
items.synopsis: The creator reports testing Gemini as a free competitor to ChatGPT and rates it highly, pointing at the Google developer interface as openly accessible. The concrete comparison he draws is a two-million-token context window against 128k for ChatGPT, alongside the Gemini 2.0 models and an experimental version. He also names unlimited file sharing and advanced customisation, with access gated behind commenting gemini.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: Six marketing sites, starting with Mojo for animated logos
items.synopsis: The caption named all six tools, Mojo App, Dzine AI, Free Ad Copy, Flow GPT, Jogg AI and Backpack Bot, and the transcript demonstrates the first. At mojoapp.com you upload a logo, in his demo the KitKat mark, and the site returns an animated version of it within seconds. The remaining five are listed but not walked through.
items.author: onlinemarket2522

items.title: Day 66: a transition tool kept secret
items.synopsis: The transcript adds almost nothing to the caption and never names the tool, which it calls only a secret AI tool. The workflow is to open it, type a prompt describing the transition you want, and wait a few minutes for the clip. The name is withheld pending a Transition comment and a follow, so entry sixty-six of the hundred-day series remains unidentifiable.
items.author: unq_ai

items.title: Kling AI puts models in your clothes for fashion marketing
items.synopsis: The creator presents a fashion-marketing shift in which Kling AI generates video of models wearing your own garments. He walks through the process end to end, from creating the model to the final animation, aimed at producing professional marketing video for a brand. The link is gated behind commenting mode.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: An unnamed product-photo-to-video tool with scene generation
items.synopsis: The transcript describes the capability without naming the website, leaving the comment gate intact. It animates existing product photography so old content can be repurposed, and the creator claims companies the size of Nike and Meta use comparable sites for their AI ads. A newer scene-generation feature takes a dropped-in image plus a text prompt and returns a video in ten to thirty seconds, with camera moves such as zoom in or zoom out added by prompt. The post is disclosed as an ad.
items.author: rourke

items.title: Fake drone shots built free in Google Earth Studio
items.synopsis: The transcript completely replaces a caption that said only follow for daily tips, and gives the whole method. Open Google Earth Studio, create a blank project, set the planet, dimensions and frame rate, then click Start; use the search icon to jump to the exact location and adjust camera position and rotation on the preview until the framing works. Scrolling down to Add Attributes and enabling time of day and clouds lets you set the lighting and weather, at which point the drone shot renders.
items.author: instacoachmike

items.title: An unnamed image-to-video model with a property use case
items.synopsis: The transcript shows the workflow without ever naming the tool, which stays behind the comment gate. You supply either a prompt or an image, in his case an AI-generated still, ask for a dynamic video, and it returns several variants in under a minute at what he calls ultra-realistic quality. The use case he develops is real estate: feed in a photograph of a room and get back a moving shot that travels through the space and its contents.
items.author: zeynebmaxim.ai

items.title: Flux 1 as a free open-source rival to Midjourney
items.synopsis: The creator presents Flux 1 as a free image generator shaking Midjourney, stressing it is entirely free and open source, and points to the Pro model on Flux pro art or the Realism LORA on Fal AI. His practical advice is to alternate between Midjourney and Flux to find the right style and to iterate generously. For animation he names Dream Machine at thirty generations a day and Kling AI at sixty credits a day as the best free options, with links gated behind commenting flux.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: A resume-matching app built with ChatGPT and v0.dev in under a minute
items.synopsis: The transcript names the stack the hashtags only gestured at. The creator describes the app he wants in ChatGPT or Claude, copies the whole answer into v0.dev, and asks it to design a React site with Tailwind CSS. The result is a working tool for recruitment agencies that takes a job description plus a hundred resumes, scores the match and outputs names, match verdicts and any field such as email. He then publishes it directly as a link and positions it as fast prototyping.
items.author: brand.nat

items.title: An unnamed free AI clothing-swap site, still behind the comment gate
items.synopsis: The transcript explains the workflow but never names the site, so the gate the caption set up is never opened. You drag in a photo of yourself and an image of the garment you want, which the creator stresses need not be an e-commerce shot but can simply be someone wearing the item, then hit run and the tool transplants the clothing with matching lighting and shadows and no Photoshop or generative fill. The name is reserved for people who comment AI.
items.author: rourke

items.title: A five-step photo restoration chain in Uniconverter AI
items.synopsis: The creator argues restoring old photos for large-format print is essential for designers and that Photoshop alone does not cut it, then gives the exact sequence. Download Uniconverter AI, open the AI image enhancer, upload the image and run Old Photo Colorize then export; re-upload that result into the image upscaler at 8X and export again. Finally run Face or Auto Enhancer to render the final version.
items.author: brothersinart1

items.title: Three lines appended to every prompt for better answers
items.synopsis: The creator shares three tricks she adds to the end of every prompt when she wants seriously good answers from ChatGPT. The caption frames the recurring questions it addresses: how to get better answers, how to tailor responses to your business and what simple tweaks raise output quality. The three lines themselves are delivered in the video.
items.author: sabrina_ramonov

items.title: NotebookLM and MapThis turn a PDF into study material
items.synopsis: The transcript identifies both tools the caption kept vague. Google NotebookLM converts any PDF into a study guide, a briefing document or an FAQ. MapThis takes the same PDF and renders it as a flowchart, or alternatively as a mind map, which is the capability the creator rates most highly.
items.author: digitalsamaritan

items.title: Kittl for printable designs sold to individual clients
items.synopsis: The creator argues the real advantage of AI tooling is the speed of producing visuals, which supports a system of bespoke creations per client across clothing, comic books, cards and anything printable, using kittl.com. The named tool is Kittl, and the business model is pairing those designs with content creation to drive traffic and sell. The link is gated behind commenting IDEA.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Two unnamed presentation generators pitched over Canva
items.synopsis: The transcript argues nobody should still be using Canva or PowerPoint given current AI tooling, and describes two products without naming either. The first generates highly attractive visuals, using AI to produce personalised presentations tailored to your field. The second is positioned as more specialised in presentations carrying animations, which the creator frames as valuable for anyone wanting motion in a deck, and both are promised only by DM.
items.author: zeynebmaxim.ai

items.title: Playground for design, plus Printify and Dream Machine
items.synopsis: The creator presents playground.com/design as a route into graphic design without technical skills, highlighting that its AI renders text correctly, long a weak point for image models, so you can talk to it and have it act as a personal designer. He then names the monetisation chain: connect printify.com to Etsy, TikTok Shop and Shopify to put designs on products and sell on autopilot. For motion he points to lumalabs.ai Dream Machine as the image animator.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Cloning yourself with a HeyGen instant avatar
items.synopsis: The creator describes having fun cloning herself using the HeyGen instant avatar feature. The tool is named explicitly and the use case is a synthetic presenter version of oneself. No workflow or quality assessment is given.

items.title: Installing Flux locally through Pinocchio in one minute
items.synopsis: The walkthrough installs Flux locally on PC or Mac with four steps: download and install the app from Pinocchio.computer, open the Explore tab, click Flux Web UI and press download, then press Start in the left menu if it does not launch itself. The first image pulls the model so it is slow, after which generation speeds up, and two variants are offered, Flux Schnell and Flux Merged. The hard requirement he states is 12 GB of video memory, with ComfyUI named as the route to run it on less.

items.title: FlutterFlow named as the app-building tool
items.synopsis: The creator names the software directly in the caption: FlutterFlow, the visual builder for Flutter applications. The rest is a subscribe request with business and development hashtags. What he builds with it is shown in the video.
